# Benchmarks

This log is append-only. Do not enter estimates or targets as measurements.
Every result must include the PDG and upstream commit SHAs, exact/fast mode,
build type and flags, machine/CPU/GPU/storage/toolkit/driver details, input hash
and point count, pipeline hash, warm/cold-cache state, sample count, median,
p5/p95, output hashes, and links or paths to raw profile artifacts.

The automatic threshold came from same-machine, pre-commit selector trials at
head `0e31fd1a9` and working-tree snapshot
`66f27b4edf3555cdf121868085e48734a2dc51694c8d70f025d66c4ff94ab8cc`.
Those decision-only trials used one warmup and five measured samples per side
and the synchronous streamed writer that preceded the final asynchronous
queue:

| Points | PDG host | Forced CUDA | CUDA/host speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1,000,000 | 0.046080 s | 0.274787 s | 0.168x |
| 4,000,000 | 0.154322 s | 0.301903 s | 0.511x |
| 8,000,000 | 0.294565 s | 0.353811 s | 0.833x |
| 12,000,000 | 0.429354 s | 0.419536 s | 1.023x |
| 16,000,000 | 0.570192 s | 0.476977 s | 1.195x |
| 21,970,934 | 0.750135 s | 0.525517 s | 1.427x |

The raw tuning reports are
`build/benchmarks/gpu-host-streamed-break-even-{1m,4000000,8000000,12000000,16000000}-dirty.json`
and `build/benchmarks/gpu-host-streamed-full-dirty.json`. A separate full-size
simple-ferry trial (`gpu-host-break-even-simple-ferry-full-dirty.json`, snapshot
`fc5e9044776aef46da368eee12f4a4a7d9e5e9c70b259157a0cf985be9718121`)
was slower on CUDA: 0.594810 s versus 0.323497 s, or 0.544x. The production
selector therefore uses a conservative 16-million-point threshold and also
requires the measured assignment/instruction density; simple translation and
simple ferry remain on the faster exact host path.

Nsight Systems 2026.1.3 profile
`build/profiles/gpu-point-program-11a90bef9.nsys-rep` (SHA-256
`04ccd5b92ca8168465ef214f415cd9ba7ce8a55e4c1627b2c239a22ba6488c2b`)
records a 221.945 ms fused NVTX range. Across 168 chunks, GPU kernels total
43.220 ms: translation 25.702 ms, exact return recount 11.118 ms, assign VM
3.707 ms, pack 2.183 ms, and decode 0.510 ms. Transfers total 30.729 ms H2D
and 36.049 ms D2H; positioned writes total 220.374 ms, identifying output I/O
and first-use pinned allocation rather than the VM kernel as the remaining
end-to-end limit. The profiled, real-time CUDA output and a same-day pinned
PDAL run were byte-identical at SHA-256
`f1b2ccbb699dc9eeb794adba755600774a05354c62d31668693f2cb389381fa1`.
Hardware performance counters were unavailable to Nsight Compute under the
driver's profiling policy, so this entry makes no roofline-percentage claim.

The forced host wrapper measured **0.909x** pinned PDAL. Every warmup and

`ff14463744dbe9ddd2f1d10271d278a7e41478e254d96a0780bda9d7aa1da2fe`;

host replacement is disabled; option-free execution keeps pinned PDAL for the
stats stage while qualified adjacent regions may remain native. CUDA runtime

measured option-free PDG at 5.848450 s versus its interleaved oracle at

default delegates the unqualified stage with only process-selection overhead;

## Unaccepted diagnostic — exact grid/BVH G1 selection matrix

- Recorded: 2026-08-07 06:43:37 UTC
- Commit: `1b1cf8187c24c0ff7e63d0986dd959dd2b2838b4`; dirty development
  snapshot, so this is not eligible for a numbered benchmark checkpoint
- Machine: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090, SM 8.9, 25,280,839,680 bytes; driver
  610.43.03, CUDA runtime/toolkit 13.3
- Mode/build: exact, Release, GCC 16.1.1, `-O3 -DNDEBUG`
- Workload: deterministic synthetic uniform-ALS, clustered-TLS, and
  mixed-density point sets; `k=16`; reusable index already resident
- Protocol: two warmups and seven measured samples per backend, alternating
  grid-first and BVH-first order; medians below are CUDA-event query time

Every row first compared the complete result buffer and status buffer from the
uniform grid and Morton BVH byte-for-byte. All comparisons passed, including
ordered neighbor-dependent means and all six ordered covariance coefficients.

| Profile/query | Points | Selector | Grid median | BVH median | Measured winner |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Uniform ALS / mean distance | 1,048,576 | grid | 55.471 ms | 1,141.179 ms | grid, 20.573x |
| Uniform ALS / covariance | 1,048,576 | grid | 56.550 ms | 1,140.486 ms | grid, 20.168x |
| Clustered TLS / mean distance | 262,144 | grid | 48.753 ms | 61.584 ms | grid, 1.263x |
| Clustered TLS / covariance | 262,144 | grid | 49.141 ms | 62.696 ms | grid, 1.276x |
| Clustered TLS / mean distance | 524,288 | Morton BVH | 239.776 ms | 158.995 ms | BVH, 1.508x |
| Clustered TLS / covariance | 524,288 | Morton BVH | 242.740 ms | 158.429 ms | BVH, 1.532x |
| Clustered TLS / mean distance | 1,048,576 | Morton BVH | 564.256 ms | 406.034 ms | BVH, 1.390x |
| Clustered TLS / covariance | 1,048,576 | Morton BVH | 563.410 ms | 408.374 ms | BVH, 1.380x |
| Mixed density / mean distance | 1,048,576 | grid | 617.267 ms | 1,251.376 ms | grid, 2.027x |
| Mixed density / covariance | 1,048,576 | grid | 617.171 ms | 1,241.313 ms | grid, 2.011x |

The original evenly spaced occupancy probe selected BVH for the 65,536-point
clustered and mixed cases even though grid was faster. It also aliases
periodically ordered sources. The corrected selector uses deterministic hashed
sample positions and selects BVH only when the sample shows broad clustering
and estimates a hot cell with at least 2,048 points. It chooses the measured
winner at every point in the table. Persistent storage at 1,048,576 points was
29,360,128 bytes for grid and 54,525,928 bytes for this power-of-two BVH; the
planner retains its conservative 76-byte/point non-power-of-two bound.

The raw reports are
`build/benchmarks/pdg-spatial-g1-{uniform-als,clustered-tls,mixed-density}-*.json`.
Their SHA-256 hashes can be regenerated with
`sha256sum build/benchmarks/pdg-spatial-g1-*.json`; the ten reports are retained
with this development build. This remains an unaccepted diagnostic because the
tree was dirty, the profiles are synthetic, and the run has no complete PDAL
process baseline. A clean-tree real-corpus and end-to-end neighborhood matrix
is still required before G1 or any stage speedup is accepted.

## B0011 — P1.5 D4 standalone placement calibration and E5 audit

- Recorded: 2026-08-07
- Implementation checkpoint: `88adde94f7efe16a8ece092468280fef843c9a40`
- Machine/build: the same AMD Ryzen 9 7900, RTX 4090/SM 89, driver 610.43.03,
  CUDA 13.3 reference configuration used by the cited source reports; exact
  Release source timings and a warnings-as-errors Host Debug model build
- Classification: B3 calibration only. This entry audits placement winners;
  it is not B1 kernel evidence, B2 acceptance, or a new stage verdict.

The frozen matrix contains 52 complete-process comparisons in 19 program
classes. Twenty-two cases come from accepted clean benchmark checkpoints,
seven are clean proposed approximate-coplanar qualification rows, and 23 are
the decision-cited diagnostics that triggered D0050. The manifest references
58 unique raw reports; every embedded SHA-256 verified against the retained
local report. Its own SHA-256 is
`b1247ca67ca4885f4a4eadaaeac8b77c5035a4505710f4e86c07af53a959f57b`.

The infrastructure coefficients are fixed measurements, not tuned stage
thresholds:

| Term | Coefficient | Source |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Cold CUDA setup | 239.214115 ms | OLS intercept of device-minus-host medians in B0005's six-row fused round-trip curve |
| Host to device | 0.038850571 ns/byte | B0005 trace: 30.729 ms over 21,970,934 36-byte records |
| Device to host | 0.045576629 ns/byte | B0005 trace: 36.049 ms over the same records |
| Canonical packing | 0.002759960 ns/byte | B0005 trace: 2.183 ms pack kernel over the same records |
| Shared-index build | 0.008297173 ns/byte | median synchronized build-wall/persistent-byte ratio over 20 D0034 grid/BVH rows |
| Synchronization | 1.930 us/call | median of 170 `cudaStreamSynchronize` calls in the retained B0005 profile |

One linear residual model per measured program class accounts for the remaining
host/device compute difference. The first unbounded fit selected device for the
measured 37,566-point approximate-coplanar host winner, producing 51/52 correct
calls (98.077%). Because this is a demonstrated placement error on the required
small negative-control surface, the model now fails closed below that class's
next measured device-winning point, 131,072. No fitted coefficient changed.
The final direct C++ audit predicts 52/52 winners (100%), exceeding E5's 90%
requirement. This includes host selection for fused point programs at one,
four, and eight million points and device selection at 12, 16, and 21,970,934
points; it also preserves the observed Morton and expression-statistics
crossovers.

The audit additionally exposed result transfers that a column-only plan would
miss. Keep masks, 64-bit permutations, splitter cell pairs, and fixed summary
records are now descriptor-declared, charged only on a spill, and included in
peak VRAM. The focused planner/placement lane passes 36/36, the registered
matrix audit passes, and the provenance command reports `verified 58/58 unique
raw reports; missing 0`.

This satisfies E5 for the matrix frozen by D0050, not D4 as a whole. Production
selection is unchanged. Executable region placement, V4 boundary reporting,
and the process-level V7 host negative control remain open.

- Protocol: identical to B0015 (one warmup, three measured samples per

Both lanes are byte-exact but statistically flat against B0015 (1.809x,
4.576x) despite D0073's 2.2–3.4x kernel wins on the 4M fixture. The
follow-up 22M measurement explains it: `knnGatherKernel` runs 32.20 s at
22M (60% of the coplanar lane wall) at 12.8% achieved occupancy with
0.39% SM and 0.01% DRAM throughput — an idle-GPU work-imbalance tail, not
a throughput limit. Isolated outlier points walk enormous empty shell
rings (the 4M prefix is spatially compact and has no such tail, which is
why every D0069–D0073 kernel figure measured there looked
throughput-bound). A forced Morton-BVH backend run is byte-identical and
brings the 22M gather to 21.73 s — better, still tail-dominated. The
D0073 optimizations are real for the dense majority of queries and stay;
the tail is the next surface (device shell budget with host repair of
the declared-incomplete rows).

scalable planner-owned cloth/Grid product and an exact composable kernel-chain
design are the appropriate future work; no placement model is added from this
result.

  ReturnNumber/NumberOfReturns are fixture invariants used by the upstream
  oracle but not materialized in this direct primitive harness. All rows report
  `classification_exact_and_staged_snapshot_consistent=true`; the independent
  unit matrix supplies raw binary64 raster parity. The selector row uses three

  build/pdg-cuda-release/bin/pdg_pmf_tiled_benchmark --warmups 5 --iterations 11 --fixture sparse --width 513 --sparse-points 256 --output build/benchmarks/pmf-fill-sparse-513-p256-v4.json

and transfer/repair only their eigensystems for the shared eigen-family path.
Keep it only if exact complete-process wall improves by roughly 5--10%; if it
does not, close this endpoint and continue the measured catalog. The retained
routing manifest is `build/benchmarks/b0069-coplanar-profile.json`, 3,814
bytes at SHA-256
`5c039498874a90956325290688304f056d1b3f585fe39c61769a7f120ef4b43c`.

dimension change, coordinate generation, or incompatible width. Missing
runtime cardinality declines to the previous exact independent query unless a
proof requirement is set. Max-k incompleteness may conservatively repair an
extra smaller-k row, but both consumers retain their pinned KD3 exact outputs.
Checked allocation arithmetic rejects size overflow before launch.

| 64 | 2.057952491 | 2.081910588 | 1.767798752 | 85.9009% | 0.0276219 |

The stage surface subtracts the fresh pinned output-shaped control,
0.290153739 seconds, which reproduces the established 40,000,701-byte
`6876e51cba9a3145a0d16a88aac819971badc771bdc668b6ea30626e8d57af92`. Every
count emits a distinct 48,000,909-byte artifact, so each is a genuinely
different computation rather than a relabelled one, and the current default
correctly delegates all of them exactly at 0.970x--0.988x.

Three measured facts decide the scope of the remaining range:

1. **Cost is strongly sub-linear in count.** Going from seven to 64 neighbors
   is 9.14x more neighbors but only 2.3241x more stock stage time, and the
   stock per-neighbor cost falls 3.93x across the range. The dominant stock
   cost is the per-query index traversal, which is largely count-independent;
   the count-dependent part is the accumulation, which is comparatively cheap.
   This matches B0139's phase capture, where 88.392121% of filter time was the
   post-index query/projection.
2. **The opportunity grows with count.** The stage share of stock wall rises
   monotonically from 72.3867% at seven to 85.9009% at 64, so wider counts are
   the *more* attractive acceleration targets, not less.
3. **The engine is already parameterized for the range.** The device
   projection accumulates over `min(groundCount, neighbors)` with no
   fixed-width state; the resident preflight already budgets
   `3 + count * (4 + 8)` bytes per point, which is 771 bytes per point and 771
   MB for this fixture at count 64; and the shared index already rejects
   `maximumNeighbors > 64`. The admissible cap of 64 is therefore the
   spatial index's own pre-existing limit rather than a new constant.

Consequently the count ladder is a **proof** ladder, not an implementation or
cost ladder. Closing counts eight through 64 one slice at a time would spend
roughly 57 further three-commit triads re-proving a structurally identical
envelope. B0143 should instead close the whole admissible range in one
parameterized envelope whose proof matrix is generated over count rather than
written per count.

Retained evidence: per-count paired reports

at 17,080/17,076/17,088/17,081/17,093/17,093/17,080 bytes, the fresh control
`build/benchmarks/b0142-hag-nn-output-control-current-clean-1m.json` at 17,100
bytes/SHA-256
`e80e13b5909cc5e54f8ca10a33ad0986d20f20111798d8f3469fa65566e3714b`, and the
complete manifest
`build/benchmarks/b0142-hag-nn-count-range-measurement-manifest.json`,
9,083 bytes/SHA-256
`6031bff39b611d98ad802b1727cd8d9cdd82ad74711f0dbd6803b0a8a837ffdb`.

Four-category record: functionally supported yes through exact pinned-PDAL
fallback at every measured count; GPU-native no above seven;
performance-qualified no; automatically selected no. This slice changes no

## B0145 — The shared BVH kNN gather is register-limited, not backend-limited

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `782d6fe35`; no product code changes. Pinned
  upstream remains `f1e35f5c3e416b8c6a2c39966c8205cfae54afe2`.
- Machine/build: Ryzen 9 7900, RTX 4090 SM89, driver 610.43.03, CUDA 13.3.73,
  Nsight Compute 2026.2.1, Release `-O3 -DNDEBUG`.
- Workload: the exact explicit `count=64` direct endpoint from B0144 on the
  retained 1,000,002-point offset-grid fixture.

B0144 reopened this endpoint because the shared `bvhKnnGatherKernel` reached
17.576763% of wall. B0145 names its limiter before any change is proposed.

**Backend selection is already correct and is not the lever.** Five alternating
same-binary runs at count 64, each with the output removed first so the
no-overwrite refusal does not mask a result:

| Backend | Median, s | Versus adaptive |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Adaptive (selects Morton BVH) | 0.476555539 | baseline |
| Forced Morton BVH | 0.477948684 | +0.2923% (noise) |
| Forced uniform grid | 0.832525226 | **+74.6964%** |

All three emit byte-identical output at SHA-256
`e210627724a51919f338c0b318bdbb54e9230673d807c03c4ab094d7f5309f4c`, so the
planner's adaptive choice is confirmed optimal at wide count and no backend
change is available.

**The kernel is compute/latency-bound and occupancy-capped by registers.** From
the B0144 count-64 capture, `bvhKnnGatherKernel` runs 82.63 milliseconds over a
15,626-block grid at 64 threads per block with 48 registers per thread. Compute
(SM) throughput is 67.00% against 49.95% memory and DRAM throughput, so it is
not bandwidth-bound. Achieved occupancy is 72.72% against an 83.33% theoretical
ceiling, and the occupancy limiters are explicit: block limit registers 20,
versus 24 for the SM limit, 24 for warps, and 32 for shared memory. Register
pressure is therefore the binding constraint — 48 registers per thread allows
only 20 blocks per SM, which is below the hardware's 24-block ceiling.

Static and dynamic shared memory per block are both zero, so shared-memory
staging is unused and is not the constraint.

The measured next hypothesis is occupancy through register pressure — a
`__launch_bounds__` or launch-shape change on this specific kernel — not a
backend change, not shared-memory staging, and not a new kernel family. B0053's
rejection of bounded launch-shape variants was measured on the *uniform-grid*
`knnGatherKernel`, whose register and occupancy profile differs, so that
negative result must be re-measured here rather than assumed to transfer.

Any change must hold the exact candidate order, tie and incompleteness status
reporting, and the host repair predicates that depend on them, across every
shared-index consumer — nndistance, LOF, statistical outlier,
approximatecoplanar, normal, the eigen family, neighborclassifier, and the HAG
family — not just HAG-NN.

Four-category record: unchanged by this slice. No product code, coverage,
model, or automatic selection changes; this is a profiling record that names a
limiter and rejects two candidate directions by measurement.

## B0146 — First reference-pipeline baseline: pdg is slower than stock on real workflows

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `5b230555a`; the only product-adjacent change in
  this slice is the new harness `scripts/pdg/benchmark_reference.py`. Pinned
  upstream remains `f1e35f5c3e416b8c6a2c39966c8205cfae54afe2`.
- Machine/build: Ryzen 9 7900, RTX 4090 SM89, driver 610.43.03, CUDA 13.3.73,
  Linux 7.1.3, NVMe/ext4, `powersave`, Release `-O3 -DNDEBUG`.
- Workload: 1,000,000 points from the retained AHN bench data, recompressed by
  the pinned oracle into `build/bench-data/reference/ref-1m.laz` (6,747,641
  bytes) and `ref-1m.copc.laz` (6,999,294 bytes). No new source data is
  introduced; LAS 36,000,375 bytes compresses 5.3x.
- Protocol: warm cache, one untimed warmup and three alternating measured pairs
  per workflow, complete-process wall clock, outputs removed before every run,
  every artifact compared byte-for-byte. Cold-cache measurement is **not**
  covered and remains open.

This is the first measurement against D0208's actual release criterion.

| Workflow | Pinned PDAL, s | `pdg` default, s | Speedup | Delta, s | Exact |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | :---: |
| `r1-translate` | 0.485255 | 0.536847 | **0.903899x** | +0.051592 | yes |
| `r2-ground-normalize` | 1.571233 | 1.602798 | 0.980306x | +0.031565 | yes |
| `r3-dtm` | 0.668329 | 0.688729 | 0.970380x | +0.020400 | yes |
| `r4-denoise-thin` | 4.624976 | 4.604383 | 1.004472x | -0.020593 | yes |
| `r5-copc-query` | 0.243936 | 0.265905 | 0.917378x | +0.021970 | yes |
| `r6-features` | 9.019737 | 9.026260 | 0.999277x | +0.006523 | yes |

**`pdg` is slower than stock PDAL on five of six reference workflows and never
meaningfully faster.** Output is byte-exact everywhere, so this is purely a
speed result. The overhead is roughly constant at +0.02 to +0.05 seconds, which
is why it is worst on the shortest and most common workflow: `r1-translate`
loses 10.6% and `r5-copc-query` 9.0%, while the 9-second `r6-features` loses
only 0.07%.

None of the qualified 2.5x--48x routes in this repository fires in any of these
six workflows. Placement stats show every one running `pdal_standard_host`.

**Why: three independent admission blockers, all engine policy rather than
algorithmic limits.** Probing a `filters.normal` pipeline on 250K points and
varying one thing at a time:

| Variation | Executor | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| plain `writers.las` | `planner_resident_shared_index` | none — accelerates |
| `extra_dims="NormalZ=float"` | `pdal_standard_host` | `invalid_runtime_facts` |
| `extra_dims="all"` | `pdal_standard_host` | `invalid_runtime_facts` |
| `compression=true` (LAZ output) | `pdal_standard_host` | `invalid_runtime_facts` |
| `normal` + `covariancefeatures` | `pdal_standard_host` | `mixed_calibration_models` |

So: writing any computed dimension blocks acceleration; writing LAZ blocks
acceleration; and chaining two neighborhood consumers blocks acceleration. Each
alone is fatal, and every realistic feature-extraction pipeline hits at least
two. `r6-features` hits all three. Writing computed dimensions is the entire
point of running a feature filter, and LAZ is the standard interchange format,
so these are not exotic shapes.

A correction to an intermediate hypothesis recorded here for honesty: an
earlier probe compared `r6` with LAZ against `r6` with uncompressed LAS, saw
0.999277x versus 0.995857x, and concluded LAZ was not a blocker. That
conclusion was wrong. LAZ output *is* a blocker; the comparison could not see
it because `r6` was already blocked twice over by `extra_dims` and mixed
calibration models. The single-variable probe above is the reliable evidence.

Two harness defects were found and fixed while producing this baseline, both
worth recording because either could have manufactured a false result:

- `readers.copc` in the pinned oracle is multi-threaded and its point order
  varies between runs — three oracle runs of `r5` produced three different
  output hashes. This is upstream non-determinism, not a `pdg` defect. The
  workflow now pins `requests=1` so it has a deterministic exact contract.
- The harness initially reported "exact" for a workflow whose runs all failed,
  because a missing artifact compared `None` to `None`. It now requires that
  artifacts actually exist and that no run returned nonzero before it will call
  a comparison exact.

Retained evidence: per-workflow reports
`build/benchmarks/b0146-r{1..6}-*-baseline-1m.json`, the single-variable
admission probe recorded in this entry, and the harness itself at
`scripts/pdg/benchmark_reference.py`.

Four-category record: unchanged. This slice changes no stage behavior. It
establishes the baseline that D0208 made the progress metric and identifies the
first three concrete targets.

## B0147 — The accelerated envelope requires an option-free uncompressed LAS writer

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `0239ebee4`; no product code changes. This is a
  root-cause analysis of B0146's baseline.
- Method: single-variable probes of a `readers.las -> filters.normal(knn=8) ->
  writers.las` pipeline on the retained 250K fixture, reading the placement
  decision from `pdg resident --stats`.

B0146 found `pdg` slower than stock on five of six reference workflows with
every workflow running `pdal_standard_host`, and D0209 attributed that to three
independent admission blockers. That attribution was too generous. The true
cause is a single rule, and it is far narrower than three blockers suggests:

| Writer | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `writers.las`, no options | **accelerates** |
| `+ a_srs` | host, `invalid_runtime_facts` |
| `+ scale_x`/`offset_x` | host, `invalid_runtime_facts` |
| `+ forward` | host, `invalid_runtime_facts` |
| `+ minor_version` | host, `invalid_runtime_facts` |
| `+ dataformat_id` | host, `invalid_runtime_facts` |
| `+ extra_dims` (named or `all`) | host, `invalid_runtime_facts` |
| `+ compression` (LAZ) | host, `invalid_runtime_facts` |

**Any writer option whatsoever disqualifies the entire pipeline from
acceleration.** `src/plan/Pipeline.cpp:2558` marks a `readers.las`/`writers.las`
stage native only when `hasOnlyOptions(node, {"type", "filename", "tag",
"inputs"})` and the filename is uncompressed LAS; `lasHeaderFacts` in
`src/cli/ResidentPipeline.cpp:1191` then refuses to produce runtime facts
unless both endpoints are native, so runtime placement reports
`invalid_runtime_facts` and the whole graph falls to unaccelerated host PDAL.

The accelerated envelope is therefore *option-free uncompressed LAS on both
ends*. Real pipelines routinely set `a_srs`, `scale_x`/`offset_x`, `forward`,
`minor_version`, `dataformat_id`, or `extra_dims`, and routinely read and write
LAZ. That is why not one qualified route fires in any reference workflow.

The two causes are not the same kind of problem, and D0209 conflated them:

- **Writer options are policy.** `a_srs`, `forward`, `minor_version`,
  `dataformat_id`, and `scale`/`offset` are header and metadata concerns that
  do not change the point-processing mathematics at all. The gate rejects them
  because the native writer only knows one canonical layout, not because the
  compute path cannot run. Widening this is admission and publisher work, and
  it is the cheapest available speed in the product.
- **LAZ is a genuine capability gap.** `src/io/las/Las.cpp:322` throws
  "compressed LAZ records require the chunk decoder", and no such decoder or
  encoder exists anywhere in the engine. LAZ cannot be admitted by relaxing a
  predicate; it needs the chunk codec that P4 has always planned. This is now
  measured justification for D0204's ranking of native I/O first, replacing the
  extrapolation that ranking previously rested on.

Correction to D0209, recorded rather than quietly amended: D0209 described all
three blockers as "engine policy rather than algorithmic limits". That is right
for writer options and wrong for LAZ, which has no codec at all. The
`mixed_calibration_models` blocker for two neighborhood consumers is a third,
separate issue and remains as described.

Four-category record: unchanged. No product code, coverage, model, or
selection changes.

## B0148 — The public command leaves 3.70x on the table

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `aecdd8749`; no product code changes retained. An
  `a_srs` admission prototype was built, measured, and fully reverted.
- Machine/build: Ryzen 9 7900, RTX 4090 SM89, Release `-O3 -DNDEBUG`, frozen
  epoch 1704067200, warm cache, three runs per executable.
- Workload: `readers.las -> filters.normal(knn=8) -> writers.las` over the
  retained 1,000,000-point bench fixture, with an option-free writer so nothing
  in the admission envelope is being stretched.

| Command | Median, s | Output SHA-256 prefix |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| pinned `pdal pipeline` | 4.372143 | `69f25352c7cd2652` |
| `pdg pipeline` (public) | 4.407116 | `69f25352c7cd2652` |
| `pdg resident` | **1.181099** | `69f25352c7cd2652` |

All three artifacts are byte-identical. The resident executor is **3.70x faster
than the public command on the same pipeline, on unmodified code, today** — and
`pdg pipeline` does not use it. The public command is 0.992x pinned PDAL, which
is exactly the profile B0146 measured across the reference workflows.

This supersedes B0147's diagnosis as the *primary* cause. B0147 correctly found
that any writer option blocks `lasHeaderFacts` and therefore resident
placement, and that finding stands for the `pdg resident` path. But it is not
what makes the reference baseline slow: even a fully option-free pipeline that
resident placement accepts is still executed unaccelerated by the public
command, because automatic selection matches a small whitelist of exact graph
shapes rather than everything resident placement can prove.

An `a_srs` admission prototype was built to test B0147's hypothesis directly. It
worked as predicted — `planner_resident_shared_index` became available and
output stayed byte-exact — but it produced no speedup through the public
command (0.993601x at 250K, 0.991722x at 1M, 1.001350x at 4M), because widening
admission does not change which command routes to the executor. The prototype is
fully reverted per the B0056/B0061/B0108 precedent for non-winning prototypes;
its measurement is the deliverable.

The measured opportunity is therefore automatic selection, not admission
options and not kernels: roughly 3.7x is already built, already exact, already
proven by four Compute Sanitizer tools, and simply not reachable from the
command users run.

Four-category record: unchanged. No product code, coverage, model, or selection
changes; the prototype was reverted.

| Command | Before, s | After, s |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| pinned `pdal pipeline` | 4.372143 | 4.410862 |
| `pdg pipeline` | 4.407116 | **1.218549** |

  That is **3.62x pinned PDAL through the public command**, byte-exact at
  `69f25352c7cd2652`. The full Release unit binary passes 577 tests with two
  optional corpus skips, and the dispatcher-boundary and resident-pipeline
  process gates pass.

- Effect on the reference pipelines, which is the D0208 release criterion:

| Workflow | B0146 baseline | With prototype |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `r1-translate` | 0.903899x | 0.935046x |
| `r2-ground-normalize` | 0.980306x | 0.993491x |
| `r3-dtm` | 0.970380x | 0.977403x |
| `r4-denoise-thin` | 1.004472x | 0.993697x |
| `r5-copc-query` | 0.917378x | 0.926887x |
| `r6-features` | 0.999277x | 0.996922x |

  All still exact, all still at or below parity. The prototype moves the
  reference set by one to three percent and wins nothing.

- Why the two results differ: every reference workflow reads and writes LAZ,
  and B0147 established that LAZ prevents `lasHeaderFacts` from producing
  runtime facts at all, so placement is unavailable and there is nothing for a
  relaxed selection gate to select. Generalized selection unlocks the
  *uncompressed option-free LAS* subset and only that subset.
- Disposition: **reverted.** It does not clear the reference-baseline gate that
  D0208 made the release criterion, and retaining it would broaden automatic
  selection to a far larger surface of graph shapes than the exactness matrices
  currently prove. D0106 restricted automatic admission to exact named shapes
  precisely because broad selection needs broad proof, and discharging that
  proof burden is a slice of its own. The measurement is the deliverable, per
  the B0056/B0061/B0108/B0148 precedent.
- Consequence for the queue: this reverses D0211's ordering. Generalized
  selection cannot help any reference workflow until LAZ is admissible, so the
  LAZ chunk codec must come first. Once it exists, this prototype becomes
  immediately valuable and its 3.62x should be re-measured on workflows that
  can actually reach it.

Four-category record: unchanged. Prototype reverted; no product code, coverage,
model, or selection changes.

## B0150 — The engine decodes LAZ byte-exactly

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: implementation on clean commit `4b8609023`.
- Change: `src/io/las/LasChunkDecoder.{hpp,cpp}` decodes a compressed LAS
  file's point records into the uncompressed layout the rest of the engine
  already understands, using the lazperf already vendored at `vendor/lazperf`
  and already built by the fork. No third-party code enters the tree, and
  `AGENTS.md` priority 5's LASzip prohibition is satisfied by construction.
- Proof: `LasChunkDecoder.DecodesLazRecordsExactlyLikeTheUncompressedFile`
  decodes all 1,000,000 records of `build/bench-data/reference/ref-1m.laz` and
  compares each against the corresponding record of the uncompressed
  `download-3101-prefix-1m.las`. Every record matches byte-for-byte, and the
  decoded buffer length matches the declared point count times record length
  exactly — a short or long decode is treated as a corrupt read rather than a
  partial success. `LasChunkDecoder.RejectsAnUncompressedFile` proves the
  inverse guard.
- Gates: the CUDA Release unit binary passes 579 tests plus the two optional
  corpus skips, and the host ASan/UBSan binary passes 388 plus the same two
  skips with the decoder exercised over the full 1M-point fixture.
- Build note: lazperf's vendored headers trip the engine's `-Werror -Wshadow
  -Wpedantic`, so `vendor/` is included as a SYSTEM directory for `pdg_core`.
  Third-party warnings are suppressed at the include boundary rather than by
  relaxing the engine's own warning contract.
- Scope, stated plainly: this slice adds the capability and proves it exact. It
  is deliberately sequential and copies the mapped view once, and it is **not
  yet wired into `FileView::pointRecord` or `lasHeaderFacts`**, so no reference
  workflow is accelerated by it yet and no speed claim is made here. lazperf's
  `reader::chunk_decompressor` exposes per-chunk decode, which is the route to
  the chunk-parallel design P4 calls for; that is a separate slice and must be
  measured rather than assumed.

Four-category record: `readers.las` LAZ input gains an exact engine-side decode
capability; GPU-native no; performance-qualified no; automatically selected no.

## B0151 — LAZ input reaches placement, byte-exact, at 3.69x

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: implementation on clean commit `0551c1f22`.
- Change: header-derived placement facts now accept a LAZ reader.
  `lasHeaderFacts` parses `.laz` public headers, requires the compression bit
  and the extension to agree, and records a new `compressedReader` fact. Every
  route that turns those facts into raw-record access — the three
  `exactDirect*` boundary branches and the direct mapped LAS source — now
  refuses a compressed reader explicitly. `.laz` shorthand also infers
  `readers.las`/`writers.las`, matching upstream PDAL.
- Result on `readers.las(ref-1m.laz) -> filters.normal(knn=8) -> writers.las`:

| Command | Median, s | Output SHA-256 prefix |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| pinned `pdal pipeline` | 4.430506 | `69f25352c7cd2652` |
| `pdg pipeline` | 4.446593 | `69f25352c7cd2652` |
| `pdg resident` | **1.199375** | `69f25352c7cd2652` |

  LAZ input now reports `planner_resident_shared_index` with placement
  available, `direct_las_resident_source` correctly unused, and output
  byte-identical to pinned PDAL — the same hash the uncompressed fixture
  produces, as it must. That is **3.69x** through `pdg resident`. `pdg pipeline`
  is unchanged because selection generalization (B0149, reverted) is still
  pending, which is exactly the split D0212 predicted.
- A bug this slice introduced and the suite caught: the first revision replaced
  the reader's `native` check with an extension-only check, which silently
  dropped `native`'s *option-free* requirement. A configured reader such as
  `count=1` would then have produced placement facts whose point count the
  header contradicts. `pdg_resident_pipeline_process` failed on exactly that
  assertion. The fix adds `FileStagePlan::optionFreeLasFamily`, which carries
  the same option-free requirement as `native` while allowing `.laz`, and
  `native` stays uncompressed-only because it additionally authorizes
  memory-mapped record access. A new `PipelinePlan.
  LasFamilyPlacementFactsRequireAnOptionFreeReader` case pins all four
  combinations of extension and configuredness so the mistake cannot return.
- Gates: CUDA Release 580 tests, host ASan/UBSan 389, both plus the two
  optional corpus skips; the dispatcher-boundary, resident-pipeline,
  radialdensity-direct, extra-double-direct, and HAG-NN CUDA process matrices
  all pass. A configured LAZ reader still fails closed with
  `invalid_runtime_facts`.

Four-category record: `readers.las` LAZ input is functionally supported through
the engine's placement path; GPU-native unchanged; performance-qualified no —
3.69x here is a single named directional pair, not a five-pair qualification;
automatically selected no.

## B0153 — Generalized selection regresses real workflows by 34%

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: implementation on clean commit `7fd9e5885`. The selection
  generalization measured here is reverted; the LAZ writer-option admission is
  retained.
- Retained change: `writers.las` with `compression:true` on a `.laz` filename
  is now admitted. B0152 proved that form byte-identical to the option-free
  `.laz` sink, so it cannot change the record layout placement budgets. Any
  other combination — `compression:false`, or compression on a `.las` name —
  stays unadmitted, because there the option genuinely decides the encoding.
- Reverted change: relaxing the three automatic-admission gates so any pipeline
  runtime placement can prove is admitted. B0149 measured this at 3.62x on
  uncompressed LAS and deferred it behind the LAZ gap. With that gap now
  closed, it was re-landed and measured against the reference baseline:

| Workflow | B0146 baseline | Generalized selection | Reverted |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `r1-translate` | 0.903899x | **0.660230x** | 0.902110x |
| `r2-ground-normalize` | 0.980306x | 0.984650x | 0.996375x |
| `r3-dtm` | 0.970380x | 0.982109x | 0.954402x |
| `r4-denoise-thin` | 1.004472x | 0.928523x | 0.997660x |
| `r5-copc-query` | 0.917378x | 0.904648x | 0.937867x |
| `r6-features` | 0.999277x | 0.996746x | 1.005921x |

  Generalized selection **regresses `r1-translate` by 34%** and `r4` by 7%. It
  is not a win being blocked by something else; it is actively harmful.
- Mechanism, measured rather than inferred: `r1` is never accelerated at all.
  Its placement is unavailable with `non_cardinality_preserving_stage` — the
  crop filter changes point count — so it runs `pdal_standard_host` either way.
  What changed is *when* it finds out. With the whitelist, a non-matching
  pipeline is rejected on cheap JSON structure before any device work. Without
  it, every such pipeline first pays runtime placement's CUDA device and
  profile discovery, measured at 0.174804 seconds in the stats capture, and
  only then declines. On a 0.7-second workflow that fixed cost is roughly a
  quarter of the wall.
- **The whitelist is load-bearing for cost, not only for proof.** D0106's
  narrow admission has been read in this session as excessive caution; it is
  also what keeps the decline path free. Any future generalization must order
  admission checks by cost — every structural test that can reject a pipeline
  without touching CUDA must run before device and profile discovery.
  `non_cardinality_preserving_stage` is exactly such a test and is currently
  evaluated after it.
- That ordering is the actionable next step, and it is worth more than
  generalized selection was: it would make declining free, which benefits every
  pipeline the engine cannot accelerate — currently most of them.
- Gates on the retained state: CUDA Release 580 tests and host ASan/UBSan 389,
  both plus the two optional corpus skips; dispatcher-boundary,
  resident-pipeline, radialdensity-direct, and extra-double-direct process
  gates pass. The reverted baseline shows no regression against B0146 and `r6`
  is marginally above parity at 1.005921x.

Four-category record: unchanged. The retained admission change adds no
selection; the generalization is reverted.

## B0154 — The constant `pdg` overhead is process startup, and NVRTC is a third of the removable part

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `62c0006f3`; no product code changes. This is a
  measurement of the fixed cost B0146 observed as a roughly constant +0.02 to
  +0.05 seconds on every reference workflow.
- Method: a trivial `readers.las -> writers.las` pipeline over 25,000 points
  isolates startup from work, `--version` isolates process load from pipeline
  execution, and trivial C programs linked against individual CUDA libraries
  attribute the load cost.

| Measurement | Median, s |
| --- | ---: |
| `pdal pipeline` (25K trivial) | 0.028292 |
| `pdg pipeline` (25K trivial) | 0.054048 |
| `pdal --version` | 0.013294 |
| `pdg --version` (dispatcher only) | 0.013943 |
| `pdg-engine --version` | 0.036196 |

The dispatcher itself is not the problem: `pdg --version` costs the same as
`pdal --version`. The engine binary costs **+0.022902 seconds** more to load
than upstream's `pdal`, which accounts for essentially all of the +0.025756
observed on the trivial pipeline.

Attribution of the CUDA share, each measured against an identical trivial
program:

| Linked | Median, s | Delta vs unlinked |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| nothing | 0.000399 | — |
| `libcudart` (0.7 MB) | 0.001230 | +0.000831 |
| `libnvrtc` (114.5 MB) | 0.005822 | **+0.005423** |
| `libcudart` + `libnvrtc` | 0.006603 | +0.006204 |
| + `libcuda` (107.4 MB) | 0.008106 | +0.007707 |

CUDA libraries account for about 7.7 milliseconds of the engine's 22.9, and
`libnvrtc` alone is 5.4 of that. NVRTC exists solely for D0076's fused JIT
envelope, which most pipelines never enter, yet it is a `DT_NEEDED` dependency
loaded eagerly in every process.

- Available saving: `dlopen`-ing NVRTC on first JIT compilation instead of
  linking it eagerly recovers about 5.4 milliseconds per process. Against the
  reference workflows that is 2.2% of `r5-copc-query`, 1.1% of `r1-translate`,
  and negligible on the long ones — individually below the repository's usual
  5--10% endpoint gate, but it is a cross-cutting cost paid by every invocation
  including those that never touch CUDA, which is the category the gate was not
  written for.
- The remaining ~15 milliseconds is the engine binary and its PDAL linkage
  rather than CUDA, and is not addressed by any change proposed here.
- Stated honestly: this measurement does not by itself make any reference
  workflow faster. It converts "pdg has a constant overhead" into a specific,
  attributed number with one identified removable component.

Four-category record: unchanged. No product code, coverage, model, or selection
changes.

## B0155 — Lazy NVRTC cuts engine startup overhead by 43%

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: implementation on clean commit `b3e721a84`.
- Change: NVRTC is resolved through `dlopen` at the first fused-JIT
  compilation instead of being a `DT_NEEDED` link dependency. Seven symbols
  are bound behind a small shim in `src/io/las/LasTranslateKernels.cu`;
  `CUDA::nvrtc` is removed from the engine's link line. A missing library or
  symbol yields no JIT, which the caller already handles as a compile failure
  and falls back from, so the failure mode is unchanged.
- Result, 25 samples per binary:

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `pdg-engine --version` overhead vs `pdal` | 0.022902 | **0.013117** |

  A **9.785-millisecond** recovery, 43% of the engine's startup overhead, and
  `ldd` no longer lists `libnvrtc` at all. The saving exceeds the 5.4
  milliseconds B0154's microbenchmark attributed to mapping the library,
  because dropping the dependency also removes its relocation and
  symbol-resolution work.
- Reference baseline, versus B0146:

| Workflow | B0146 | B0155 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `r1-translate` | 0.903899x | 0.927326x |
| `r2-ground-normalize` | 0.980306x | 0.993634x |
| `r3-dtm` | 0.970380x | 0.977296x |
| `r4-denoise-thin` | 1.004472x | 0.995213x |
| `r5-copc-query` | 0.917378x | 0.936423x |
| `r6-features` | 0.999277x | 0.991691x |

  Five of six improve; the movements are one to two percent, consistent with a
  fixed ten-millisecond saving against workflows of 0.24 to 9 seconds. This
  does not turn any workflow into a win and is not claimed to.
- Correctness: `CudaLasPointProgram.FusedJitSpecializesEveryAdmittedFormat`
  still compiles a specialization for every admitted LAS record format, taking
  310 milliseconds of real compilation, so the JIT is genuinely exercised
  through the shim rather than silently skipped. The CUDA Release binary passes

  and the dispatcher-boundary, resident-pipeline, extra-double-direct,
  native-translate-format-3, and fused assign/ferry process gates pass.
- Remaining: about 13 milliseconds of engine startup overhead survives, which
  B0154 attributed to the engine binary and its PDAL linkage rather than to
  CUDA. `libcudart` (+0.83 ms) and `libcuda` (+1.50 ms) are genuinely needed
  whenever CUDA is used and are not candidates for the same treatment.

Four-category record: unchanged. No stage behavior, coverage, model, or
selection changes.

## B0157 — `extra_dims` admission is a calibration question, not a facts question

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `f88f314da`. The prototype described here is fully
  reverted; no product code change is retained.
- Prototype: admit writer `extra_dims` to header-derived placement facts,
  composing it with B0152's redundant `.laz` compression allowance so a sink
  carrying both is admitted, and budget the wider output record conservatively
  from the prepared layout's point size rather than the canonical 36-byte
  constant.
- It worked mechanically. A `filters.normal(knn=8)` pipeline writing
  `extra_dims=all` moved from `pdal_standard_host`/`invalid_runtime_facts` to
  `planner_resident_shared_index`, and the two reference workflows blocked on
  this moved from `invalid_runtime_facts` to genuine placement decisions:
  `r2-ground-normalize` to `missing_calibration_model`, which is correct
  because SMRF has no model and measures 0.599x on CUDA, and `r6-features` to
  `mixed_calibration_models`, the known D0077 rule. Output stayed byte-exact
  throughout and the reference baseline was unchanged within noise.
- **Reverted, because an existing process gate objects for a reason the
  prototype did not answer.** `resident_pipeline_process_test.py` asserts that
  a writer carrying `extra_dims` must report `invalid_runtime_facts`, with the
  stated rationale that writer options "change the packed output layout and are
  not represented by the default-format calibration". The conservative
  budgeting added here addresses *memory*, but the placement calibration
  predicts device-versus-host *timing* from record sizes measured on the
  canonical layout. A wider output changes transfer time, so admitting it
  selects the device using a model whose envelope no longer covers the shape.
  That is the condition `OutsideCalibrationEnvelope` exists to name.
- The disciplined resolution is not to edit the assertion to match the code.
  The test documents a deliberate decision; the prototype had no evidence
  against it. `extra_dims` therefore belongs with the calibration work
  alongside `mixed_calibration_models`, not with the admission relaxations that
  LAZ needed.
- What this changes about the plan: item 1 of the D0208 work order listed
  `extra_dims` as an admission and publication question. It is not. Admitting
  it requires either a calibration measured over the wider output record, or a
  placement decision that is robust to output width. `readers.copc` and
  `writers.gdal`, the other two entries in that item, are untested against this
  objection and may face the same one.

Four-category record: unchanged. Prototype reverted; no product code, coverage,
model, or selection changes.

## B0158 — `non_cardinality_preserving_stage` is a catch-all, and it misreports

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `e306ee871`; no product code changes. This is a
  diagnostic finding that corrects the plan written in `f88f314da`.
- Method: single-filter `readers.las -> filter -> writers.las` pipelines over
  the 250K fixture, each run through `pdg resident --stats` with the refusal
  read directly.

| Pipeline | Refusal |
| --- | --- |
| `filters.crop` (2D bounds) | `non_cardinality_preserving_stage` |
| `filters.range` (`Z[0:200]`) | `non_cardinality_preserving_stage` |
| `filters.sample` (radius 1.0) | `non_cardinality_preserving_stage` |
| `filters.expression` (`Z > 0`) | `non_cardinality_preserving_stage` |
| `filters.reprojection` | `non_cardinality_preserving_stage` |

Two of these results contradict what the codebase says about itself.

**`filters.reprojection` preserves cardinality.** It cannot change point count,
yet it reports a cardinality refusal. The cause is that
`StageDescriptor::fusion.cardinalityPreserving` defaults to `false`
(`include/pdg/Plan.hpp:123`), so every stage that does not explicitly declare
itself preserving — which includes every unsupported stage compiled to
`FallbackStagePlan` — is treated as cardinality-changing. The refusal therefore
means "some stage is not *known* to preserve point count", not "some stage
changes point count". Those are very different statements, and the reported one
is wrong.

**`filters.expression` is listed as automatically selected** in
`docs/stage-coverage.md`, compiles to a `PredicateProgram`, and is exactly the
declared-predicate shape the cardinality exemption exists to admit — yet it is
refused in the simplest possible pipeline. Whatever the exemption admits, it is
not admitting a bare predicate between a plain reader and a plain writer.

- Correction to the plan: item 2 of the work order claimed that expressing
  `crop`, `range`, and `sample` as declared predicates would unblock `r1` and
  `r4`. That is not established. `crop` and `range` *already* compile to
  `PredicateProgram` with `native = true` and a device residency preference
  (`src/plan/Pipeline.cpp:2687` and `:2715`), and they are refused anyway. The
  work is not to express them as predicates; it is to find why the existing
  exemption does not fire, and to separate the two conditions the refusal
  currently conflates.
- Also relevant to `r1`: it contains `filters.reprojection`, so even a complete
  fix for cardinality-changing filters would not admit it. Any pipeline
  containing an unsupported stage is refused whole, reported as a cardinality
  problem. That is a much broader constraint than the plan recorded.
- Next: B0159 should split the refusal into two distinct reasons — a stage that
  declares a cardinality change without a qualifying predicate, versus a stage
  whose properties are unknown because it is unsupported — and then determine
  why the declared-predicate exemption does not admit a bare
  `filters.expression`. Diagnosis before implementation: this session has now
  corrected eight attributions, and every one came from measuring rather than
  reading.

Four-category record: unchanged. No product code, coverage, model, or selection
changes.
