| `crop` 2D bounds | 1 | **0** | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| `expression` `Intensity > 100` | 1 | **1** | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| `range` `Intensity[100:200]` | 1 | **1** | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 |

Every clause passes for all five. The exemption fails on exactly one:
`preferredResidency == MemoryKind::Device`.

Plan-time residency comes from `predicateSupportsExactDevice(program)`
(`src/stages/Assign.cpp:600`), which calls
`exactDeviceExpression(expression, /*allowCoordinateLoads=*/false)`. **Any
predicate reading X, Y, or Z is therefore planned to Host**, fails the
exemption, and refuses the entire pipeline.

Confirmed end to end: `filters.range` on `Intensity` reaches
`missing_calibration_model`, a genuine placement decision, where the identical
filter on `Z` reports `non_cardinality_preserving_stage`.

- The conservatism has a real basis. A coordinate load is exact on device only
  when the column is binary64, or signed-32 with a zero scale offset, which is
  a property of the runtime batch rather than of the plan. The two-argument
  `predicateSupportsExactDevice(batch, program)` overload checks precisely that
  and already exists. The plan-time check lacks a batch, so it assumes the
  worst.
- The consequence is disproportionate. `filters.crop` is *inherently* a
  coordinate predicate and can never be placed under this rule; neither can
  `filters.range` on Z, nor `filters.sample`. Those are among the most-used
  filters in PDAL, and a single conservative argument makes every pipeline
  containing one unplaceable in full — reported, per B0158, under a reason that
  describes a different condition.
- Direction for a fix, not taken here: the repository's established pattern is
  to declare optimistically at plan time, verify against the real batch at
  runtime, and fail closed to the exact host path — which is exactly what the
  two-argument overload is for. Applying that pattern to coordinate predicates
  would let placement consider them while keeping the exactness guarantee at
  the point where it can actually be checked. That is a placement-semantics
  change and needs its own slice, its own proofs, and a reference-baseline
  measurement.
- Retained: `tests/unit/predicate_residency_test.cpp` pins the current
  behaviour for both coordinate and non-coordinate predicates, so a future
  change to it is deliberate and visible rather than silent. CUDA Release now
  passes 582 tests and host ASan/UBSan 391, both plus the two optional corpus
  skips.

Four-category record: unchanged. Characterization test only.

## B0160 — The declare-then-verify fix has a probe-fidelity hazard

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `2a1c5e717`; no product code changes. This
  completes B0159's diagnosis with the constraint an implementer must satisfy.
- B0159 established the fix direction: stop refusing coordinate predicates at
  plan time and let the existing runtime checks decide. Before attempting it,
  the two runtime checks were examined, and they do not behave the same way.

  1. **The resident preflight** (`src/pdal/PdgResidentContext.cpp:268`) calls
     `predicateSupportsExactDevice(probe, program)` and **throws** on failure.
     Under automatic admission a throw before commitment returns to the
     unchanged public selector, so this is a clean fail-closed fallback.
  2. **The device evaluator** (`src/stages/AssignKernels.cu:476`) makes the
     same call and also throws — but it runs *during* execution, after
     commitment, where a throw is an error rather than a fallback.

  So the safety of an optimistic plan-time declaration rests entirely on the
  preflight rejecting anything the evaluator would later reject.

- **The probe is not faithful on the property that matters.** It is constructed
  at `src/pdal/PdgResidentContext.cpp:203` with
  `CoordinateEncoding({1.0, 1.0, 1.0}, {0.0, 0.0, 0.0})` — a **zero** scale
  offset. The runtime exactness rule accepts a signed-32 coordinate column only
  when its offset is zero, so the probe represents the most permissive possible
  case. Real LAS data does not: the retained AHN fixtures carry offsets around
  184500 and 494923.
- The hazard is therefore concrete. If any resident path presents coordinates
  as signed-32 rather than binary64, an optimistic plan-time declaration would
  pass the preflight against a zero-offset probe and then throw inside
  `evaluatePredicateDevice` on real data — converting today's graceful host
  fallback into a hard failure, after commitment, on exactly the most common
  filters in PDAL.
- There is good reason to believe the engine always materializes binary64 XYZ
  — B0051 hydrates mapped LAS coordinates into binary64 columns and
  `projectHagNnColumn` requires binary64 XYZ — in which case the first clause
  of the rule is satisfied and the offset never matters. **That belief is not
  evidence.** It must be verified against the real resident path before the
  plan-time check is relaxed, and the verification belongs with the change.
- Implementer's checklist for the fix, in order: confirm every resident path
  materializes coordinates as binary64; make the preflight probe model the real
  coordinate encoding rather than a zero offset, so probe and evaluator agree;
  only then relax plan-time residency; and gate on the heavy physical process
  lanes as well as the reference baseline, because the failure mode is a
  post-commitment error on ordinary data rather than a wrong number.

Four-category record: unchanged. Analysis only; no product code, coverage,
model, or selection changes.

## B0161 — The probe hazard is closed: probe and execution lane share an encoding

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `d12bc35e5`; no product code changes. This
  discharges the first item of B0160's implementer checklist.
- B0160 identified the risk in relaxing plan-time predicate residency: the
  resident preflight probe is built with a zero coordinate offset, while real
  LAS data carries large offsets, so an optimistic plan-time declaration might
  pass preflight and then throw inside `evaluatePredicateDevice` after
  commitment — converting a graceful fallback into a hard failure.
- **The hazard does not apply.** The resident execution lane constructs its own
  `PointBatch` at `src/pdal/PdgResidentContext.cpp:1409` with
  `CoordinateEncoding({1.0, 1.0, 1.0}, {0.0, 0.0, 0.0})` — the identical
  encoding the preflight probe uses at `:204`. Probe and evaluator therefore
  agree by construction rather than by coincidence: whatever the probe accepts,
  the executing batch presents the same coordinate encoding, so the runtime
  exactness rule reaches the same answer.
- Both clauses of that rule are satisfied for the resident lane regardless of
  which one applies: coordinates are materialized as binary64 in the
  neighborhood paths (`src/pdal/PdgNeighborhood.cpp:424`, `:848`, `:1009`),
  and even a signed-32 column would pass because the lane's offset is zero.
  The file's real offsets — around 184500 and 494923 in the retained AHN
  fixtures — never reach the batch encoding; they are absorbed when
  coordinates are hydrated.
- Consequence for B0162: the second checklist item, making the probe model the
  real coordinate encoding, is **not** needed as a prerequisite. The probe is
  already faithful to the lane it is predicting. What remains is the change
  itself — relaxing plan-time residency for coordinate predicates — plus its
  proofs and the heavy physical process lanes, which are still warranted
  because the failure mode after commitment is an error rather than a wrong
  number.
- Stated as a limit rather than a claim: this verifies the *resident* lane. It
  does not verify every non-resident path that might evaluate a predicate on
  device, and B0162 should confirm there is no such path before relying on
  this.

Four-category record: unchanged. Verification only; no product code, coverage,
model, or selection changes.

## B0162 — Coordinate predicates are placeable; `crop` and `range` reach a real decision

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: implementation on clean commit `d6cdbed51`.
- Change: `predicateMaySupportExactDevice` permits coordinate loads at plan
  time, and the `filters.crop` and `filters.range` compile sites use it. The
  column question is deferred to the two places that can answer it against a
  real batch — the resident preflight, which fails closed before commitment,
  and `evaluatePredicateDevice`.
- Safety established before the change, not assumed after it. B0161 showed the
  resident lane builds its batch with the same zero coordinate offset as the
  preflight probe; B0162 extended that check to every other device
  predicate-evaluating path — `PdgPointProgramFilter` (`:723`, `:851`, `:1000`)
  and the fused LAS translate lane (`LasTranslateKernels.cu:2198`) — and all of
  them use a zero offset too. Probe and evaluator therefore agree everywhere,
  so an optimistic plan-time declaration cannot become a post-commitment error.
- Result: `filters.crop` and `filters.range` on `Z` now pass the
  declared-predicate exemption and reach `missing_calibration_model` — the same
  genuine placement decision the identical filter on `Intensity` already
  reached — instead of the misleading `non_cardinality_preserving_stage`. The
  cropped output is byte-identical to pinned PDAL at `14200985bbf86937`.
- **Reference baseline is unchanged** (`r1` 0.939589x, `r4` 0.999023x, `r6`
  0.999933x) and both workflows still refuse, because each contains a *second*
  blocker this slice does not address: `r1` also has `filters.reprojection`,
  which is unsupported and trips the same catch-all refusal (B0158), and `r4`
  also has `filters.sample`, which is not a predicate at all. That is stated
  plainly rather than presented as a partial win: the change removes one of two
  blockers from each workflow and moves neither into acceleration.
- Deliberately not widened: `filters.expression`. It carries
  `placementModel = "point-program"` and feeds the fused point-program
  selection paths, so relaxing its residency has a materially larger blast
  radius and deserves its own slice and measurement.
  `PredicateResidency.CoordinateExpressionIsStillPlannedToHost` pins that
  asymmetry so it reads as a decision rather than an oversight.
- The characterization test written in B0159 did its job: it asserted the old
  Host residency, failed when this change landed, and was updated deliberately
  rather than silently.
- Gates: CUDA Release 583 tests and host ASan/UBSan 391, both plus the two
  optional corpus skips; dispatcher-boundary, resident-pipeline,
  extra-double-direct, fused assign/ferry, and — most relevant here — the
  `hybrid_crop_2d_host_exact` and `hybrid_range_fused_host_exact` exactness
  lanes all pass.

Four-category record: `filters.crop` and `filters.range` become placement
candidates rather than automatic refusals; GPU-native unchanged;
performance-qualified no; automatically selected no.

## B0163 — Split the catch-all refusal; `sample` was never a cardinality problem

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: implementation on clean commit `12ef3d879`.
- Change: `RuntimePlacementUnavailableReason::UnsupportedStage` is added and
  `planStructureRefusal` reports it for a stage that is not implemented
  natively, keeping `NonCardinalityPreservingStage` for a native stage that
  genuinely declares a cardinality change without qualifying as a declared
  predicate. Behaviour is unchanged — both still refuse — only the reason is
  now accurate.
- Why it mattered: `fusion.cardinalityPreserving` defaults to `false`
  (`include/pdg/Plan.hpp:123`), so every unsupported fallback stage reported a
  cardinality problem it does not have (B0158). `filters.reprojection`, which
  cannot change point count, reported exactly that. This session's plan was
  misdirected three separate times by reasons that described a different
  condition from the one that fired.

| Filter | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `filters.reprojection` | `non_cardinality_preserving_stage` | `unsupported_stage` |
| `filters.sample` | `non_cardinality_preserving_stage` | `unsupported_stage` |
| `filters.crop` | `non_cardinality_preserving_stage` | `missing_calibration_model` (B0162) |
| `filters.expression` on `Z` | `non_cardinality_preserving_stage` | `non_cardinality_preserving_stage` |

- Immediate correction to the plan: **`filters.sample` is not a cardinality
  problem at all** — it is simply unsupported. The work order said `r4` needed
  cardinality-changing stages expressed as declared predicates; what `r4`
  actually needs is a native `filters.sample`. Both reference workflows still
  refusing now report `unsupported_stage`, which names the real remaining work:
  `r1` needs `filters.reprojection`, `r4` needs `filters.sample`.
- `filters.expression` on `Z` legitimately keeps the cardinality reason: it is
  native, declares a cardinality change, and is still planned to Host by B0162's
  deliberately narrow scope. The reason is now true of exactly the case it
  names.
- One existing assertion changed. `RuntimePlacement.
  KeepsUncomposedOrRepeatedCardinalityChangesUnavailable` expected the
  host-fallback `where` form to report the cardinality reason. `hasOnlyOptions`
  excludes `where`, so that form compiles to a fallback with `native == false`
  and its cardinality behaviour is unknown rather than known-bad; it now
  reports `UnsupportedStage`. The refusal is unchanged and only the label moved,
  which is the purpose of this slice — unlike B0157, where a failing gate
  encoded a substantive constraint and the prototype was reverted instead.
- Gates: CUDA Release 583 tests and host ASan/UBSan 391, both plus the two
  optional corpus skips; dispatcher-boundary, resident-pipeline,
  extra-double-direct, fused assign/ferry, and crop-2d exactness lanes pass.

Four-category record: unchanged. Diagnostic accuracy only; no stage behavior,
coverage, model, or selection changes.

## B0164 — `filters.sample` matters for what it blocks, not what it costs

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `214733374`; no product code changes. B0163 named
  the real remaining work for `r1` and `r4` as native `filters.reprojection`
  and `filters.sample`. D0208 requires measuring before implementing, so both
  were ablated against the pinned oracle on the 1M LAZ fixture before either is
  scheduled.

**`r4-denoise-thin`**, median of three per variant:

| Variant | Median, s | Attributed |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| full | 4.577148 | — |
| without `filters.sample` | 4.129814 | `sample` = 0.447334 s, **9.8%** |
| without `filters.outlier` | 0.893614 | `outlier` = 3.683534 s, **80.5%** |

The dominant cost is `filters.outlier`, and **this repository already has a
qualified CUDA path for it** — B0088 measured 21.389523x on an explicit 1M
composition and B0124 qualifies the standalone statistical shape at
6.521497x/10.739669x. That path cannot run here for one reason: `filters.sample`
is unsupported, and an unsupported stage refuses the entire pipeline
(B0158/B0163).

So the case for implementing `filters.sample` is not its own 9.8%. It is that a
9.8% stage is withholding an already-built, already-proven acceleration from the
80.5% next to it. That is a far stronger justification than "sample is slow",
and it is the opposite of what a cost-ranked queue would have chosen.

**`r1-translate`**, same method:

| Variant | Median, s | Attributed |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| full (crop then reproject) | 0.482196 | — |
| without `filters.reprojection` | 0.265198 | `reprojection` = 0.216998 s, **45.0%** |
| without `filters.crop` | 1.142377 | crop *saves* 0.660181 s |

Reprojection is 45% of `r1`'s wall, but unlike outlier it has no existing fast
path, and it is a PROJ/GDAL coordinate transform whose exactness depends on
datum grids and library internals — a bridge candidate under D0019 rather than
a kernel. Note also that `crop` *reduces* total wall by 0.66 seconds by
discarding points before reprojection and the writer, which is why the naive
reading of these ablations is misleading: removing a filter can make a pipeline
slower.

- Priority this establishes, against the plan's current order: `filters.sample`
  before `filters.reprojection`. Sample unlocks a measured 21x on 80.5% of a
  reference workflow; reprojection is 45% of a shorter one with nothing built
  to unlock and a much harder exactness story.
- A cheaper alternative worth testing first: `r4` might not need a native
  `sample` at all if the planner can place the *prefix* of a pipeline up to an
  unsupported stage rather than refusing the whole graph. That would unlock
  outlier's existing path without implementing anything new, and would
  generalize to every pipeline containing one unsupported stage — which,
  per B0163, is most of them. That is the measurement B0165 should make.

Four-category record: unchanged. Measurement only; no product code, coverage,
model, or selection changes.

## B0165 — Prefix placement would not help: calibration coverage is the next wall

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `27a3d94ba`; no product code changes.
- Hypothesis under test (from B0164): `r4` might not need a native
  `filters.sample` at all if the planner could place the pipeline *prefix* —
  `outlier` and `range` — and leave the unsupported `sample` on the host. That
  would have unlocked outlier's qualified 21.389523x on 80.5% of `r4`'s wall
  with nothing new implemented.
- **The hypothesis is false, and the reason is more useful than the
  hypothesis.** Split into two processes, the prefix measures 4.045113 seconds
  in pinned PDAL and 3.988288 in `pdg` — **1.014x, not accelerated at all**.
  Prefix placement cannot unlock an acceleration that does not engage for the
  prefix on its own.
- Why it does not engage, measured by narrowing the shape:

| Pipeline | Refusal |
| --- | --- |
| `outlier` + `range`, LAZ in | `missing_calibration_model` |
| `outlier` alone, LAZ in | `missing_calibration_model` |
| `outlier` alone, uncompressed LAS in | `missing_calibration_model` |
| `outlier` + `nndistance(kth,k=10)`, uncompressed LAS in | `missing_calibration_model` |

  The last row is close to B0088's qualified composition and still finds no
  model. B0092's automatic envelope is the exact
  `mean_k=8,multiplier=2,class=7 -> nndistance(kth,k=10)` default-LAS shape, so
  the models are keyed at **option level**, not at stage-sequence level. A
  pipeline missing `class=7`, or ending at a writer instead of an assign, is a
  different shape as far as calibration is concerned.
- This is the same wall B0157 hit from the other side. Admitting writer
  `extra_dims` was blocked because the placement calibration is measured on the
  canonical output layout; admitting `outlier` here is blocked because no model
  covers the shape. Two independent attempts, one conclusion: **after admission
  and refusal accuracy are fixed, calibration coverage is what stands between
  the reference workflows and the accelerations that already exist.**
- Consequence for the plan: implementing `filters.sample` natively is no longer
  justified by B0164's reasoning, because the 80.5% it was supposed to unlock
  does not currently accelerate anyway. Both `sample` and the calibration
  question would have to be solved for `r4` to move, and calibration is the
  larger and more reusable of the two — it gates `extra_dims`, `outlier` here,
  and every route in D0204's automatic-selection candidate list, all of which
  were found blocked on a calibrated model plus a fail-closed predicate.
- Honest limit: this measures `pdg resident`, which bypasses automatic
  selection. It establishes that *placement* finds no model for these shapes.
  It does not establish that the qualified B0088/B0092 routes are broken —
  those were measured on their exact named shapes and there is no evidence
  against them here.

Four-category record: unchanged. Measurement only; no product code, coverage,
model, or selection changes.

## B0166 — Calibration covers 35 models; the reference workflows need 13 stages, 10 uncovered

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `f201cf563`; no product code changes. This is the
  measurement B0165 said must precede any calibration work: what does a model
  have to cover before one is built.
- `test/data/pdg/placement-calibration-sm89.json` carries 35 stage models, 35
  pipelines, and 152 cases. Mapping them against the stages the six reference
  workflows actually contain:

| Workflow | Stage coverage |
| --- | --- |
| `r1-translate` | `crop` **none**, `reprojection` **none** |
| `r2-ground-normalize` | `smrf` **none**, `hag_nn` **none** |
| `r3-dtm` | `smrf` **none**, `range` **none**, `writers.gdal` **none** |
| `r4-denoise-thin` | `outlier` composition-only, `range` **none**, `sample` **none** |
| `r5-copc-query` | `readers.copc` **none**, `stats` covered |
| `r6-features` | `normal` covered, `covariancefeatures` covered |

  Thirteen distinct stages appear across the six workflows. Three are covered.
- **The `outlier` entry is the sharpest finding.** There is no standalone
  `outlier` model at all — only `outlier-nndistance-direct-compose`. That is
  why B0165 measured `missing_calibration_model` for `filters.outlier` alone on
  both LAZ and uncompressed LAS: placement is not rejecting the shape, it is
  finding no model to reject it with. The same pattern holds for three other
  composition models with no standalone equivalent:
  `eigen-family-compose`, `radius-outlier-radialdensity-direct-compose`, and
  `rank-optimal-compose`. Only `approximatecoplanar` has both.
- This explains `r6` as well. `normal` and `covariancefeatures` each have their
  own model, and D0077 refuses two measured models in one region by design —
  `mixed_calibration_models`. There *is* an `eigen-family-compose` model for
  exactly that pairing, but it is keyed to B0075's three-consumer,
  three-assignment shape, so a two-consumer pipeline matches neither the
  per-stage models nor the composition model.
- What a calibration program must therefore cover, in the order the evidence
  supports:
  1. **Standalone models for stages that only have composition models** —
     `outlier` first, since it is 80.5% of `r4` and already has a qualified
     21.389523x implementation waiting behind the missing model.
  2. **Composition models that generalize over consumer count**, so
     `normal + covariancefeatures` is not refused for being two of the three
     stages `eigen-family-compose` was measured on.
  3. **Models for the stages with none**, weighted by reference-workflow
     presence: `range` and `crop` appear twice each, `smrf` twice.
- What it should *not* do, on this evidence: build models for `smrf`, `pmf`,
  or `csf`. They are measured negative (0.599x, 0.583x, 0.289x) and a model
  would correctly select host anyway. Their absence from the calibration file
  is not a gap.
- Honest limit: this counts *presence* of a model, not whether an existing
  model's envelope covers a given pipeline's size or options. B0157 showed the
  second failure mode is real and separate — `extra_dims` is refused by a model
  that exists but was measured on a different output layout. A complete
  calibration plan must address both.

Four-category record: unchanged. Measurement only; no product code, coverage,
model, or selection changes.

## B0167 — Standalone `outlier` calibration ladder

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `79833f885`. This slice adds a ladder script and
  measurement rows only. **No model is fitted and no selection envelope is
  admitted** — those are behavioral changes and are deliberately left for a
  separate decision.
- Rationale: B0166 found there is no standalone `outlier` model, only
  `outlier-nndistance-direct-compose`, which is why placement reports
  `missing_calibration_model` for the stage that is 80.5% of `r4-denoise-thin`'s
  wall and already carries a qualified 21.389523x implementation. A model needs
  a ladder; this is the ladder.
- Protocol matches `calibrate-eigen-family.sh` (D0067): forced hybrid-CUDA
  against the complete pinned-PDAL process, one warmup and three runs per size,
  frozen time, byte-identical outputs required at every point. Script retained
  at `build/diagnostics/profile-work/calibrate-outlier.sh`.

| Points | Pinned PDAL, s | Forced CUDA, s | Speedup | Host ns/point |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 50,000 | 0.206651 | 0.267278 | **0.773x** | 4133.0 |
| 250,000 | 0.973985 | 0.339349 | 2.870x | 3895.9 |
| 1,000,000 | 3.956684 | 0.600461 | 6.589x | 3956.7 |
| 2,000,000 | 7.979494 | 0.944761 | 8.446x | 3989.7 |
| 4,000,000 | 16.135653 | 3.262016 | **4.947x** | 4033.9 |

Every row is byte-exact against pinned PDAL.

- The ladder has the shape a placement model needs: a clear break-even between
  50,000 and 250,000 points, and a device win of 2.9x--8.4x above it. Host cost
  is close to linear at 3896--4134 nanoseconds per point across an 80x size
  range, which is what makes a `host_ns_per_point` term fittable.
- **The 4M row is the interesting one and should not be smoothed over.**
  Speedup rises 0.773x, 2.870x, 6.589x, 8.446x and then *falls* to 4.947x. Host
  time stays linear, so the regression is on the device side: forced CUDA
  triples from 0.944761 to 3.262016 seconds for twice the points. That is the
  signature of exact host repair engaging, which the record already documents
  for this family — B0089 found a 4M incomplete-mean host-repair cliff and
  B0090/B0091 fixed the *NNDistance* side of it. Whether the standalone
  statistical-outlier path has the same cliff, and whether the existing parallel
  repair covers it, must be established before a model is fitted: a model fitted
  through this point would mispredict on both sides of it.
- Next, in order: determine what happens at 4M — repair counters are already
  published in the stats output, so this is a read rather than an experiment;
  then extend the ladder to 8M and 16M to see whether the curve recovers or
  continues down; then fit. Fitting first would bake the cliff into the
  coefficients.

Four-category record: unchanged. Ladder measurement only; no model, coverage,
or selection changes.

## B0168 — The outlier cliff is a step, not a slope, and four causes are excluded

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `b9af6db89`; no product code changes.
- B0167 found the ladder rising to 8.446x at 2M then falling to 4.947x at 4M,
  and said the repair counters could simply be read. **That was wrong and is
  corrected here:** those counters are published by the *resident* executor,
  while the ladder measures the *hybrid* per-stage path. Asking `pdg resident`
  for them returns `pdal_standard_host` with null repair blocks, because
  placement still finds no model (B0166). The claim was made from memory of the
  stats schema rather than from a run.
- Extending the ladder answers the shape question:

| Points | Pinned PDAL, s | Forced CUDA, s | Speedup | Host ns/pt | **CUDA ns/pt** |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 50,000 | 0.206651 | 0.267278 | 0.773x | 4133.0 | 5345.6 |
| 250,000 | 0.973985 | 0.339349 | 2.870x | 3895.9 | 1357.4 |
| 1,000,000 | 3.956684 | 0.600461 | 6.589x | 3956.7 | 600.5 |
| 2,000,000 | 7.979494 | 0.944761 | 8.446x | 3989.7 | **472.4** |
| 4,000,000 | 16.135653 | 3.262016 | 4.947x | 4033.9 | **815.5** |
| 8,000,000 | 32.370720 | 6.493723 | 4.985x | 4046.3 | **811.7** |

  Device cost per point *steps* from 472 to ~813 nanoseconds between 2M and 4M
  and then stays flat. It is a mode change that switches on once and remains
  on, not a progressive degradation — which matters, because a model fitted
  across it would mispredict on both sides while a model fitted per-regime
  would not.
- Four candidate causes are excluded by measurement:
  1. **Index backend.** At 4M, adaptive is 798.4 ns/pt and forced uniform grid
     801.6, so adaptive already chooses grid; forced Morton BVH is worse at
     1063.2. At 2M the same holds (486.0 adaptive, 461.2 grid, 965.1 BVH). The
     backend does not switch across the step.
  2. **The grid path itself is where the step lives** — forced grid alone goes
     461.2 to 801.6 ns/pt, reproducing it without any adaptive decision.
  3. **Tiling.** `ResidentTilePoints` is 131,072, so every size from 250K up is
     already multi-tile; nothing changes at 4M.
  4. **Host-side density effects.** Host cost per point is flat at
     3896--4046 ns across the whole 160x range, so the fixtures are not getting
     harder in a way that would explain a device-only step.
- What remains, and what B0169 should test: a device-memory or work-partition
  threshold crossed between 2M and 4M — at 4M the kNN candidate arrays alone
  are about 144 MB at D0073's 36 bytes per point, before columns and scratch.
  An Nsight Compute capture at 2M and 4M would show directly whether the gather
  changes occupancy, spills, or launch count, and that is a profile rather than
  another guess.
- The practical consequence stands regardless of cause: **a standalone
  `outlier` model must be fitted per regime, or bounded below 4M**, and the
  ladder now has the rows to do either.

Four-category record: unchanged. Measurement only.

## B0169 — The outlier step is host-side; device kernels are 4.6% of it

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `569d28925`; no product code changes.
- B0168 excluded the index backend, tiling, and host-side density as causes of
  the 2M-to-4M step, and named a device-memory or work-partition threshold as
  the leading hypothesis, to be settled by a profile rather than a guess. This
  is the profile: Nsight Compute captures of the forced-CUDA hybrid outlier
  pipeline at both sizes.

| | 2M | 4M | Ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Launches | 17 | 17 | 1.00x |
| All kernels | 31.383 ms | 134.674 ms | 4.29x |
| `knnGatherKernel` | 30.851 ms | 133.582 ms | **4.33x** |
| Complete process | 0.944761 s | 3.193439 s | 3.38x |

- **The leading hypothesis was wrong, and the profile says so plainly.** Launch
  count is identical at 17, so there is no work-partition change and no extra
  pass. The gather kernel *is* superlinear — 4.33x the time for 2x the points,
  15.4 to 33.4 nanoseconds per point — which is a real finding about the
  bounded shell walk under higher candidate density. But it is not what makes
  the ladder step.
- **Arithmetic that settles it:** the process grew 2.248678 seconds between 2M
  and 4M while all device kernels together grew 0.103291 seconds. Kernels
  account for **4.6%** of the regression. At 4M every kernel in the pipeline is
  134.674 milliseconds of a 3.193439-second process — 4.2% of wall. The other
  95.4% of the step is host-side work inside the hybrid wrapper.
- That returns the investigation to where B0167 first pointed and B0168 could
  not check: exact host repair. The outlier family has documented form here —
  B0089 found a 4M incomplete-mean host-repair cliff and B0090/B0091 fixed the
  NNDistance side of it, leaving the standalone statistical path unaddressed.
  A step that switches on between 2M and 4M and then holds flat per point is
  consistent with repair engaging for a size-dependent but then saturating
  fraction of rows.
- What B0170 needs, stated so the next attempt does not repeat B0168's mistake:
  the repair counters exist only on the resident executor, which will not run
  this shape until it has a calibration model — the very thing this ladder was
  measuring for. The way out is not another stats read. It is either to
  instrument the hybrid wrapper's repair path directly, or to measure the
  standalone outlier route through `pdg resident` with placement forced rather
  than calibrated, which the existing `PDG_REQUIRE_*` proof switches already
  support for other families.
- Unchanged practical consequence: a standalone `outlier` model must be fitted
  per regime or bounded below 4M. The cause of the regime boundary is now known
  to be host-side, which means a model that ignores it would misattribute
  host cost to the device.

Four-category record: unchanged. Profile only; no product code, coverage,
model, or selection changes.

## B0170 — Repair is part of the outlier step, but not most of it

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `0cc235c8e`; no product code changes. B0169 left
  the choice between instrumenting the hybrid wrapper and forcing placement;
  neither was needed, because the shell budget already controls the variable of
  interest without touching code.
- Method: `PDG_KNN_DEVICE_SHELL_BUDGET` bounds the device walk and therefore how
  many rows are declared incomplete and sent to exact host repair (D0074). The
  repair path builds a full host `KD3Index` per call
  (`src/pdal/PdgNeighborhood.cpp:3246`), so if repair drives the 2M-to-4M step,
  raising the budget should flatten it.

| Size | Budget 32 (default) | Budget 256 | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2M | 472.0 ns/pt | 443.4 ns/pt | -6.1% |
| 4M | 810.4 ns/pt | 679.2 ns/pt | **-16.2%** |

- **Repair is real, size-dependent, and insufficient as an explanation.**
  Raising the budget helps 4M nearly three times as much as 2M, which is
  consistent with more incomplete rows at the larger size and with the KD3
  rebuild being the expensive part. But the step survives: at budget 256 the
  4M cost is still 1.53x the 2M cost per point, where a flat regime would show
  parity. Repair accounts for part of the gap, not the bulk of it.
- Running total for the 2M-to-4M step, all measured rather than inferred:
  device kernels 4.6% (B0169), exact host repair roughly 16% at 4M (this
  slice), and the remaining majority still unattributed and host-side.
- What is now excluded: index backend, tiling, host-side input density
  (B0168), work-partition or launch-count change (B0169), and repair as a
  sufficient cause (this slice). What remains unexamined is the rest of the
  hybrid wrapper — transfers, PointView marshalling, and column
  materialization — which the existing telemetry does not cover for the
  non-resident path.
- B0171 should therefore add stats-only telemetry to the hybrid wrapper, the
  same additive pattern B0046, B0049 and B0095 used for other paths, rather
  than continue narrowing by ablation. Four slices of ablation have taken the
  unexplained share from 100% to roughly 80%; instrumenting is now the cheaper
  route to the rest.
- Unchanged practical consequence: a standalone `outlier` model must be fitted
  per regime or bounded below 4M. Nothing measured so far changes that, and the
  ladder already has the rows for either choice.

Four-category record: unchanged. Measurement only; no product code, coverage,
model, or selection changes.

## B0171 — The hybrid and resident outlier paths are different implementations

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `6fc07a12e`; the instrumentation attempted here is
  fully reverted, because it was added to the wrong function.
- Intent: add stats-only phase timing to the hybrid statistical-outlier wrapper
  to attribute the ~80% of the 2M-to-4M step that B0168--B0170 left
  unexplained. The telemetry was written into
  `tryCudaStatisticalOutlier` in `src/pdal/PdgNeighborhood.cpp` and produced no
  output at either size.
- **The reason is the finding.** `tryCudaStatisticalOutlier` has exactly one
  call site — `src/pdal/PdgOutlierFilter.cpp:370` — and it sits inside the
  branch guarded by `requireResidentExecutionContext()`. The hybrid path calls
  something else entirely: `tryStatisticalCuda`, a private member of the filter
  at `src/pdal/PdgOutlierFilter.cpp:241`. **The hybrid and resident statistical
  outlier lanes are separate implementations, not one implementation reached
  two ways.**
- This invalidates an assumption underneath B0167. That ladder was collected
  with `--candidate-mode hybrid-cuda`, so it measured `tryStatisticalCuda`. A
  placement calibration model governs whether the *resident* executor is
  selected, and the resident executor runs `tryCudaStatisticalOutlier`. **The
  ladder measures a different implementation from the one a model built on it
  would govern.** Whether the two have similar cost curves is unknown and was
  never checked; B0167 implicitly assumed one implementation.
- It also explains B0168's dead end cleanly: the repair counters really are
  resident-only, because the repair code carrying them lives in the resident
  implementation. The hybrid implementation has its own repair path and its own
  absence of telemetry.
- A concrete, testable cause for the remaining step is now visible in the
  hybrid implementation. `tryStatisticalCuda` allocates a fresh pinned host
  memory resource and a fresh device memory resource **per call**
  (`PdgOutlierFilter.cpp:255-262`), where the resident lane reuses
  planner-owned allocations. Page-pinning cost scales with size and is not
  linear, which fits a host-side step that switches on and then holds flat per
  point. That is a hypothesis with a named mechanism and a named line, not
  another guess at a category.
- Next, in order: (1) confirm the allocation hypothesis by timing
  `makeCudaPinnedMemoryResource` and the batch gather at 2M and 4M — the
  telemetry belongs in `tryStatisticalCuda`, not the resident function; (2)
  re-collect the ladder against the resident implementation, with placement
  forced rather than calibrated, since that is the implementation a model
  governs; (3) only then fit.

Four-category record: unchanged. The instrumentation is reverted; no product
code, coverage, model, or selection changes.

## B0172 — Allocation is not the cause either; the hybrid lane now has telemetry

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: implementation on clean commit `7f9e9f87e`.
- Change: stats-only phase timing in `tryStatisticalCuda`
  (`src/pdal/PdgOutlierFilter.cpp`), gated on
  `PDG_DEBUG_HYBRID_OUTLIER_PHASES`, printed to stderr so it cannot contaminate
  a byte-compared artifact. This is the additive pattern of
  `PDG_DEBUG_FUSED_JIT`. B0171 established that this lane is a separate
  implementation from the resident one and carries no telemetry of its own,
  which is why B0168--B0170 could only narrow the cost step by ablation.
- **B0171's hypothesis is disproved.** It proposed that the per-call fresh
  pinned and device memory resources explained the host-side step, since
  page-pinning scales non-linearly:

| Phase | 2M | 4M | Growth |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `pinned_resource` | 0.000001 s | 0.000001 s | none — the resource is lazy |
| `host_gather` | 0.165698 s | 0.199745 s | +0.034047 s |
| `device_resource` | 0.026391 s | 0.050425 s | +0.024034 s |
| **instrumented total** | 0.192090 s | 0.250171 s | **+0.058081 s** |

  Creating the pinned resource costs a microsecond at both sizes because it
  allocates nothing until used. The three phases together grow by 58
  milliseconds against a process step of 2.248678 seconds — **2.6%**. The
  mechanism was named and specific, which made it testable, and it is wrong.
- Running attribution of the 2M-to-4M step, all measured: device kernels 4.6%
  (B0169), exact host repair roughly 16% at 4M (B0170), allocation and host
  gather 2.6% (this slice). Roughly three quarters remains unattributed, and it
  is downstream of the marks placed here — in the gather call, the status scan
  and repair, or the mean/stddev finale.
- The telemetry is **retained** rather than reverted. Unlike B0171's attempt it
  is in the correct function, it is the instrumentation B0171 identified as
  missing, and the next attribution step needs more marks in the same place
  rather than a different technique. Both build configurations pass with it
  present: CUDA Release 583 tests, host ASan/UBSan 392, plus the two optional
  corpus skips, and the outlier direct process gate passes.
- Next: extend the marks past `device_resource` through the gather call, the
  status scan and repair, and the finale. Three quarters of a well-bounded step
  is a small target once the timing is inside the function rather than around
  it. Then re-collect the ladder against the *resident* implementation, which
  is the one a calibration model governs (B0171), before fitting anything.

Four-category record: unchanged. Diagnostic telemetry only, off by default; no
stage behavior, coverage, model, or selection changes.

## B0173 — The outlier step is the host KD3 rebuild, and it is B0089's cliff

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: implementation on clean commit `0ce0f7f96`. Extends B0172's
  telemetry through the gather, status scan, repair and finale.
- **The step is fully explained.** Phase timings for the hybrid statistical
  outlier lane:

| Phase | 2M | 4M |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `pinned_resource` | 0.000001 | 0.000001 |
| `host_gather` | 0.153066 | 0.205050 |
| `device_resource` | 0.025796 | 0.050439 |
| `gather_submit` | 0.041002 | 0.147806 |
| `gather_wait` | 0.000075 | 0.000784 |
| `status_scan` | *branch not taken* | 0.000362 |
| **`kd3_build`** | ***branch not taken*** | **1.622082** |
| `repair_and_finale` | 0.000188 | 0.001138 |

  At 2M the repair branch never executes at all — there are no incomplete rows,
  so `kd3_build` produces no mark. At 4M incomplete rows appear and the lane
  builds a full host `KD3Index` over four million points, costing 1.622082
  seconds. Against a process step of 2.248678 seconds that is **72%**, and with
  device kernels at 4.6% (B0169) the attribution is now closed.
- **This is B0089's cliff, on the path B0090/B0091 did not fix.** The record
  already documents a 4M incomplete-mean host-repair cliff; B0090 repaired
  NNDistance rows in parallel from resident coordinates and B0091 made that the
  default, qualifying the 4M route at 48.758796x. The statistical outlier
  lane's *hybrid* implementation was never given that treatment and still falls
  back to a full KD3 rebuild.
- It also explains B0170 exactly. Raising `PDG_KNN_DEVICE_SHELL_BUDGET` from 32
  to 256 cut 4M by 16.2% because a deeper device walk leaves fewer incomplete
  rows, but some remain, and one remaining row is enough to pay the entire KD3
  build. That is why the saving was real but partial, and why the step did not
  vanish.
- Recorded honestly: B0167's original hypothesis — that exact host repair
  explained the cliff — was right. It took B0168 through B0172 to measure it,
  because the counters that would have shown it belong to a different
  implementation (B0171), and four intervening hypotheses of mine were wrong.
  The conclusion is the same one guessed at the start; the difference is that it
  is now measured, quantified at 72%, and attached to a named line of code.
- Consequences, in order of value:
  1. The standalone `outlier` ladder in B0167 has a **repair cliff, not a
     scaling curve**, above 2M. A model fitted across it would encode a host
     KD3 rebuild as if it were device cost.
  2. The fix is known and precedented: apply B0090/B0091's bounded parallel
     repair from resident coordinates to the statistical outlier lane. That is
     a real implementation slice with an existing pattern to follow.
  3. Only after that should the ladder be re-collected — and against the
     *resident* implementation, which is the one a calibration model governs
     (B0171).
- Gates: CUDA Release 583 tests and host ASan/UBSan 392, both plus the two
  optional corpus skips.

Four-category record: unchanged. Diagnostic telemetry only, off by default.

## B0174 — 1.646 seconds to repair one point

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: implementation on clean commit `32db3479e`. Adds an
  incomplete-row count to the existing hybrid-lane telemetry.
- **The 4M outlier cliff is one incomplete row.**

| Size | Incomplete rows | `kd3_build` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 2M | **0** | branch not taken |
| 4M | **1** | **1.646093 s** |

  At 4M exactly one point of four million has an incomplete bounded device
  search, and repairing that single point costs a full host `KD3Index` build
  over the entire view — 1.646 seconds, 72% of the 2M-to-4M step.
- **The repository has solved this exact problem before, on a different lane.**
  B0049 measured "a 2.061175139-second compatibility KD3 repair for one
  incomplete row" on NNDistance; B0050 repaired it from resident coordinates,
  and B0064's bounded multi-block kernel cut it to 2.232480 milliseconds. The
  same shape has been sitting in the statistical outlier hybrid lane since.
- **The resident lane would already handle it.** Its device repair is gated on
  `neighbors <= 16 && incompleteRows <= 16`
  (`src/pdal/PdgNeighborhood.cpp:3171-3174`). Here `neighbors` is `mean_k + 1`
  = 9 and `incompleteRows` is 1, so both bounds are satisfied with room to
  spare — the resident lane takes the device path and never builds a KD3.
  Only the hybrid implementation, which B0171 showed is a separate code path,
  falls back to the rebuild.
- Consequences, which change the recommended slice:
  1. **The B0167 ladder is not measuring a scaling curve above 2M; it is
     measuring one unrepaired point.** Fitting a calibration model across it
     would encode a 1.6-second host KD3 rebuild as device cost, for a condition
     that depends on data rather than size.
  2. **The fix is not new work.** Give the hybrid lane the bounded device
     repair the resident lane already has, following B0090/B0091/B0064. Or, if
     only real pipelines matter under D0208, do nothing to the hybrid lane at
     all: it is reached by `PDG_EXPERIMENTAL_CUDA_HYBRID`, not by the default
     path a user runs.
  3. **The ladder must be re-collected against the resident implementation**
     before any model is fitted (B0171), and that lane is expected to show no
     cliff at all for this reason.
- The honest reading of the whole B0167--B0174 chain: a ladder was collected to
  build a calibration model, and eight slices of measurement established that
  the ladder measures the wrong implementation, encodes a data-dependent repair
  event as a size effect, and would have produced a model that mispredicts the
  code it governs. No model was fitted, which was the correct outcome.
- Gates: CUDA Release 583 tests and host ASan/UBSan 392, both plus the two
  optional corpus skips.

Four-category record: unchanged. Diagnostic telemetry only, off by default.

## B0175 — The resident lane stays unreachable, and that is the finding

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `04662fd15`; no product code changes.
- Goal: establish whether the *resident* outlier lane suffers B0174's one-row
  KD3 cliff, without adding a force switch. B0092's composition is documented
  as automatically selected, so reconstructing it from the record should reach
  the resident lane with no new machinery.
- Reconstruction, following D0204's description of B0092's envelope —
  `filters.outlier(method=statistical, mean_k=8, multiplier=2, class=7)` then
  `filters.nndistance(mode=kth, k=10)` then an assign to `UserData`, writing
  default LAS:

| Size | Pinned PDAL | `pdg` | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2M | 16.3666 s | 16.3409 s | 1.002x |
| 4M | 33.0374 s | 33.0257 s | 1.000x |

  **It is not accelerated.** A faithful-looking reconstruction of a composition
  this repository qualified at 20.300698x runs at parity, which means it did
  not match the admission envelope.
- Two readings, and the evidence does not separate them: either the
  reconstruction differs from B0092's exact shape in some option or stage
  detail not captured in the prose record, or the envelope is narrower than the
  record describes. Both point at the same underlying problem B0166 measured —

  reliably reproduce.** A qualified route that cannot be reconstructed from its

  ones actually engage.

## B0176 — Auditing the "automatically selected" column: two of four engage

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `285456f3a`; no product code changes.
- B0175 found that a reconstruction of B0092's qualified composition ran at
  parity, raising the question of how much of the "automatically selected"
  column is reachable in practice. This audits four of those entries by
  reconstructing each from its recorded description and running it through the
  **public** `pdg pipeline`, which is what "automatically selected" means.
- All four on the retained 1,000,000-point fixture:

| Route | Pinned PDAL | `pdg pipeline` | Measured | Recorded claim | Engages |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | :-: |
| `lof(minpts=10)` + assign | 8.5257 s | 1.0791 s | **7.901x** | 9.597x at 4M (B0043) | **yes** |
| `approximatecoplanar(knn=8)` + ferry | 4.1242 s | 1.0120 s | **4.075x** | 4.231x at 1M (B0097) | **yes** |
| `nndistance(kth,k=10)` + assign | 4.2953 s | 4.3081 s | 0.997x | 5.229x at 4M (B0045) | **no** |
| `mortonorder` | 0.5744 s | 0.5583 s | 1.029x | listed automatic | **no** |

- **The column is partly accurate and partly not, and now it is known which.**
  `approximatecoplanar` reproduces its recorded 1M figure almost exactly —
  4.075x measured against 4.231x recorded — which is a strong confirmation that
  the envelope, the record, and the reconstruction all agree. `lof` engages at
  7.901x on 1M against a 9.597x record at 4M; different size, same behaviour,
  consistent.
- **`nndistance` is the informative failure.** Driven through `pdg resident` it
  reports `planner_resident_shared_index` with placement available, so
  *placement* accepts the shape. Through the public command it runs at parity.
  Placement availability and automatic selection are therefore separate gates,
  and this route passes the first and fails the second — the same split B0148
  measured from the other direction, now observed on a route the coverage table
  marks automatic.
- `mortonorder` fails at placement instead, with `missing_calibration_model`,
  despite also being marked automatic.
- What this establishes, stated carefully: two documented envelopes are
  reachable from their records and deliver close to their recorded figures; two
  are not reachable from their records by reconstruction. It does **not**
  establish that the latter two are broken — B0045 and the Morton work were
  measured on exact shapes whose full detail may not survive prose, which is
  precisely B0175's point. The distinction that matters for planning is
  *reachability*, not correctness, and reachability is what a user gets.
- Recommended follow-up: extend this audit to the remaining automatic entries
  (`estimaterank`/`optimalneighborhood`, `radiusassign`, `radialdensity`, the
  eigen family, `expressionstats`, the point-program stages), and annotate the
  coverage table with a reachability mark distinct from the qualification mark.
  A route that is qualified but unreachable is not delivering speed to anyone,
  which is exactly what D0208 made the criterion.

Four-category record: unchanged by this slice; it measures the existing
"automatically selected" column rather than altering it.

## B0178 — The audit converges: two gates, and one withholds a measured 3.6x

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `b51c6b5fd`; no product code changes.
- B0177 recommended generalizing the composition models over consumer count.
  **That recommendation was wrong and is withdrawn here**: claiming a model
  measured on three consumers applies to two is an envelope extension without
  measurement, which is exactly what B0157's process gate objects to and why
  that prototype was reverted. Narrowing by measurement first was the correct
  move instead.
- Narrowing the eigen family by consumer count:

| Shape | Executor | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `normal` alone | `planner_resident_shared_index` | none |
| `normal` + 1 assign | `planner_resident_shared_index` | none |
| `normal` + `eigenvalues` + 2 assigns | `pdal_standard_host` | `mixed_calibration_models` |
| 3 consumers + 3 assigns | `pdal_standard_host` | `mixed_calibration_models` |

  One neighborhood consumer is admitted; two or more never are.
  `eigen-family-compose` does not match any of these reconstructions, so
  B0075's 10.257x route requires a shape detail the record does not convey.
- **The whole audit now resolves into two independent gates.** Placement
  decides whether a shape has a usable calibration; automatic selection decides
  whether the public command uses it. Every result in B0176--B0178 sits in one
  of four cells, and the interesting cell is the third:

| | Selection admits | Selection refuses |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Placement admits** | `lof` 7.901x, `approximatecoplanar` 4.075x, point program 7.492x | **`normal`+assign, `nndistance`** |
| **Placement refuses** | — | eigen family, rank/optimal, `mortonorder` |

- **The third cell is the finding.** `normal` + assign measures 4.4416 seconds
  in pinned PDAL, 4.4609 through the public `pdg pipeline`, and **1.2273
  through `pdg resident` — 3.62x, byte-exact**. Placement already accepts it.
  The resident lane already delivers it. Only the automatic-selection whitelist
  withholds it, and `nndistance` sits in the same cell (B0176). This is the
  same 3.62x B0149 measured and reverted, now confirmed on a second route and
  with its blocking gate isolated.
- That makes the cheapest large win in the product precisely the item B0149
  deferred and B0156 unblocked: **generalizing automatic selection is worth
  ~3.6x on single-consumer neighborhood pipelines, the cost objection is gone
  (B0156 made declining free), and only the proof burden remains.** Discharging
  that burden — broadening the exactness matrices to cover what selection would
  newly admit — is a well-defined slice, not an open question.
- Recorded as a correction to my own recommendation: B0177's suggested next
  step would have extended a calibration envelope without evidence. One slice
  of measurement replaced it with a better-founded and larger target.

Four-category record: unchanged. Measurement only.

## B0179 — The selection proof burden is discharged for the isolated class

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: implementation on clean commit `e8f855f95`.
- B0178 isolated the class where placement already accepts and the resident
  executor already delivers ~3.6x byte-exactly, but the public command
  withholds it: one neighborhood consumer followed by an assign. B0149 measured
  that generalization and reverted it on two objections; B0156 removed the cost
  objection by making a declining pipeline free; the remaining objection was
  that generalized selection would run the resident executor on graphs the
  exactness matrices do not cover.
- **This slice discharges that burden and nothing else.** It adds
  `tests/differential/resident_selection_matrix.py`, registered as
  `pdg_resident_selection_matrix_cuda_exact`. **No selection gate is flipped
  and no default behaviour changes** — that is a user-facing decision and is
  deliberately left separate. The proof is worth paying either way: it covers a
  lane that already runs today via `pdg resident`.
- Coverage: five neighborhood consumers — `normal`, `eigenvalues`,
  `covariancefeatures`, `nndistance`, and `approximatecoplanar` — crossed with
  three assignment targets chosen for distinct physical widths (`UserData`
  unsigned byte, `Intensity` unsigned short, `PointSourceId` unsigned short via
  a different column). Fifteen cases, each run twice: once through pinned
  upstream PDAL and once through `pdg resident`, the executor a generalized
  selection would choose. **All fifteen are byte-identical.**
- The matrix fails rather than skips when a case is exact but ran
  `pdal_standard_host`. A shape that quietly stops reaching the resident lane
  is precisely the regression this matrix exists to catch, and a silent skip
  would hide it. That check earned itself immediately: the first fixture, a
  60x60x12 grid of 43,200 points, sat below the placement models' 250,000-point
  floor, so seven cases were exact but ran on the host. The fixture is now
  150x150x12 = 270,000 points, above the floor, and all fifteen exercise the
  intended lane.
- The fixture is generated by the pinned oracle inside the test rather than
  taken from unversioned bench data, so the matrix is self-contained and runs
  on a clean checkout.
- Gates: the new matrix passes in 36.62 seconds; the CUDA Release unit binary
  is unchanged at 583 tests plus the two optional corpus skips.
- What remains for a generalization, stated so the boundary is unambiguous:
  flipping the three admission gates B0149 identified
  (`src/cli/ResidentPipeline.cpp:2691`, `:2747`, `:3232`), then re-running this
  matrix, the reachability audit (B0176/B0177), and the reference baseline.
  The proof that blocked it is now in place.

Four-category record: unchanged. Test coverage only; no stage behavior,
coverage, model, or selection changes.

## B0180 — Generalized selection preempts the fused lane and costs 7.5x

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `b7e63da03`; the generalization measured here is
  fully reverted.
- With B0156 having removed the cost objection and B0179 the proof objection,
  the three admission gates B0149 identified were flipped and the reachability
  audit re-run through the **public** `pdg pipeline` on the 1M fixture. Every
  route stayed byte-exact.

| Route | Before | After | |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `nndistance` + assign | 0.997x | **7.338x** | recovered |
| `normal` + assign | 0.996x | **4.001x** | recovered |
| `lof` + assign | 7.901x | 8.227x | unchanged |
| `approximatecoplanar` + ferry | 4.075x | 4.141x | unchanged |
| `estimaterank` + `optimalneighborhood` | 0.982x | 0.978x | still refused |
| eigen family, three consumers | 1.025x | 0.981x | still refused |
| `mortonorder` | 1.029x | **0.742x** | **regressed 28%** |
| **`assign` + `ferry` (point program)** | **7.492x** | **1.041x** | **regressed 86%** |

- **The generalization recovers two routes and destroys the most valuable one.**
  `assign` + `ferry` are the most-used filters in PDAL and B0177 measured them
  at 7.492x through the default command. Generalized selection takes them from
  7.492x to 1.041x — an 86% loss on the shape a typical user is most likely to
  run. `mortonorder` loses 28% the same way.
- Cause: those pipelines were already being served by the **fused
  point-program lane**, which is a different and faster mechanism than the
  resident executor. Once selection stops requiring a named shape, the resident
  executor is chosen for graphs the fused lane was handling better, and
  preempts it. Nothing became incorrect — every route stayed byte-exact — the
  planner simply started choosing a worse path.
- **This is a better objection than either of the two that came before it.**
  B0149's cost objection was real and B0156 fixed it. B0179's proof objection
  was real and the fifteen-case matrix discharged it. This one is different in
  kind: generalized selection is not merely unproven on new shapes, it is
  *actively wrong* on shapes that already had a better answer. No amount of
  additional exactness coverage would have revealed it, because the failure is
  a performance choice, not a correctness one.
- It also validates running the full reachability audit rather than only the
  reference baseline. **None of the six reference workflows contains a bare
  `assign` + `ferry` pipeline**, so the reference baseline alone would have
  shown this change as harmless and it would have shipped.
- What a correct generalization must do, now that the shape of the problem is
  known: prefer the fused point-program lane where it applies, and fall to the
  resident executor only for graphs the fused lane cannot serve. That is a
  ranking between two accelerated paths, not an admission question, and it is a
  different slice from the three gates B0149 identified.
- Reverted per the B0056/B0061/B0108/B0148/B0149 precedent. The measurement is
  the deliverable: `pointprog` returns to 7.439x and `mortonorder` to 1.026x
  after the revert, and the unit binary is unchanged at 583 tests.

Four-category record: unchanged. Prototype reverted; no product code, coverage,
model, or selection changes.

## B0181 — Ranked selection: two routes recovered, the fused lane preserved

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: implementation on clean commit `1a1e8aaae`.
- B0180 showed that removing the automatic-admission whitelist outright
  recovers `nndistance` and `normal` + assign but lets the resident executor
  preempt the faster fused point-program lane, costing `assign` + `ferry` 86%.
  The fix it named was a ranking between two accelerated paths, not an
  admission change.
- Change: automatic admission is generalized, **and ranked**. A plan that
  declares neither a neighborhood query nor a grid product is a pure point
  program, which the fused lane already serves faster, so the resident executor
  declines it (`planDeclaresNeighborhoodRegion` / `planDeclaresGridRegion`).
  Every fail-closed mechanism is untouched.

| Route | Before | After | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `nndistance` + assign | 0.997x | **8.641x** | **+767%** |
| `normal` + assign | 0.996x | **3.990x** | **+301%** |
| `lof` + assign | 7.901x | 8.016x | +1.5% |
| `approximatecoplanar` + ferry | 4.075x | 4.095x | +0.5% |
| `assign` + `ferry` (fused lane) | 7.492x | 7.353x | −1.9%, noise |
| `mortonorder` | 1.029x | 1.027x | flat |
| `estimaterank` + `optimalneighborhood` | 0.982x | 0.974x | still refused |
| eigen family, three consumers | 1.025x | 0.979x | still refused |

  Every route is byte-exact. `assign` + `ferry` and `mortonorder` were measured
  over seven runs each to separate noise from regression: 7.353x median against
  a 7.492x baseline, and `pdg resident` reports `outside_calibration_envelope`
  for the point program, confirming the fused lane still owns it.
- **This does not move the release criterion, and is not claimed to.** The six
  reference workflows measure 0.939079x, 0.983750x, 0.971473x, 0.997713x,
  0.934460x and 0.998655x — unchanged within noise, because each is blocked by
  something else entirely: unsupported stages (B0163), writer options (B0147),
  or `mixed_calibration_models` (B0177). D0208 makes reference-pipeline wall
  clock the release criterion precisely so that wins elsewhere cannot be
  mistaken for progress against it.
- Retained anyway, on this reasoning: the change costs nothing measurable
  anywhere, is byte-exact on every route tested, passes every gate including
  B0179's fifteen-case selection matrix, and recovers two shapes —
  `nndistance` + assign and `normal` + assign — that are ordinary
  feature-extraction pipelines a user would plausibly write. Declining to
  retain a free, proven improvement because the six-workflow reference set
  happens not to contain it would be the mirror-image error of claiming it as
  release progress.
- Gates: CUDA Release 583 tests, host ASan/UBSan 392, both plus the two
  optional corpus skips; dispatcher-boundary, resident-pipeline,
  extra-double-direct, fused assign/ferry, crop-2d exactness, and the
  resident-selection matrix all pass.

Four-category record: `filters.nndistance` and single-consumer neighborhood
compositions become automatically selected in the ordinary resident envelope;
GPU-native unchanged; performance-qualified for the named 1M routes measured
here; the fused point-program lane retains priority where it applies.

## B0182 — The eigen-family envelope is unreachable even with source access

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `708d6446d`; no product code changes.
- B0177 found the three-consumer eigen family refused with
  `mixed_calibration_models` and B0178 measured that one neighborhood consumer
  is admitted while two or more never are. B0166 found `eigen-family-compose`
  exists as a model. This slice reads `measuredEigenFamilyRegion` in
  `src/plan/RuntimePlacement.cpp:190` and reconstructs its envelope exactly.
- The envelope is far more specific than any record conveys: six stages,
  `filters.normal(knn=12)`, `filters.eigenvalues(knn=12, normalize=true)`,
  `filters.covariancefeatures(knn=12, mode=raw, feature_set=Dimensionality)`,
  and **one** `filters.assign` stage carrying exactly
  `Classification = Linearity * 10`, `Intensity = Curvature * 1000`,
  `UserData = Eigenvalue0 * 100`. B0177's reconstruction used `knn=8` and three
  separate assign stages, which is why it missed.
- **Reconstructing all of that from the source still does not match.** The
  corrected pipeline measures 0.984x and reports `mixed_calibration_models`.
  A compiled-plan dump confirms every condition that is externally visible is
  satisfied: six stages, one resident region, all four filter stages native,
  device-preferred, and in region 0, with `covariance->neighbors == 12` and
  `mode == Raw`.
- The remaining candidates are the conditions a dump cannot show —
  `normal->alwaysUp`, `eigenvalues->normalize`, the exact
  `CovarianceDimensionality` feature constant, or `sameAssignProgram` against
  the compiled reference assignments. Identifying which would need
  instrumentation inside the matcher.
- **The finding is more useful than the speedup would have been.** B0175
  observed that a qualified route could not be reconstructed from its prose
  record. This is stronger: it cannot be reconstructed from *the source code
  that defines it*, by transcribing every literal in the matcher. An envelope
  that precise is not a route users can reach; it is a route that exists only
  for the exact artifact it was measured on.
- That reframes item 3 of the work order. "Broaden calibration coverage" is not
  primarily about adding models — `eigen-family-compose` and
  `rank-optimal-compose` already exist and are already measured. It is about
  the matchers being keyed so tightly that the models they gate are
  unreachable. A model that matches one literal pipeline delivers the same
  value as no model at all, and costs more to maintain.
- Recommended: before adding any calibration model, decide what a matcher may
  key on. Point count, record format, stage sequence, and options that change
  cost are defensible; exact assignment *expressions* are not, since they
  cannot change the cost of the neighborhood work the model actually predicts.
  Relaxing `sameAssignProgram` to a cost-equivalence check rather than a
  program-equality check would be the smallest experiment, and it is
  measurable against the recorded 10.257x.

Four-category record: unchanged. Investigation only; no product code, coverage,
model, or selection changes.

## B0183 — The eigen family is reachable: one non-default option gated 10.134x

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `33556e4ef`; no product code changes.
- B0182 concluded the eigen-family envelope was unreachable even when every
  literal in `measuredEigenFamilyRegion` was transcribed from source. **That
  conclusion was wrong, and this slice finds the missing condition.**
- The matcher requires `!normal->alwaysUp`. `filters.normal`'s `always_up`
  option **defaults to true**, so a pipeline must explicitly set
  `"always_up": false` to match. Every reconstruction until now used the
  default and was refused.
- With that one option added, the envelope engages and delivers:

| | Pinned PDAL | `pdg pipeline` | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| eigen family, `always_up=false` | 14.4171 s | 1.4227 s | **10.134x, byte-exact** |

  Against B0075's recorded **10.257x** — agreement to within 1.2%. The route,
  the model, and the record are all correct and always were.
- **What was actually wrong was my method, twice.** B0177 missed on `knn=8` and
  three assign stages. B0182 fixed those, transcribed every literal it could
  see, still failed, and concluded the envelope was unreachable *in principle*.
  The real cause was an option the matcher tests but the pipeline never
  mentions, because its default is the opposite of what the envelope needs. A
  compiled-plan dump could not show it: `alwaysUp` lives inside the
  `NormalProgram` payload, and the dump printed only stage-level fields.
- Corrections this forces, recorded rather than quietly amended:
  - B0182's headline — "unreachable even from its own source" — is withdrawn.
    It is reachable, and the source does define it; I did not read the whole
    condition list carefully enough.
  - B0182's recommendation to relax `sameAssignProgram` to cost-equivalence is
    **not** supported by this evidence. That matcher was never the blocker, and
    relaxing it would have widened an envelope without cause.
  - B0177's reachability verdict for the eigen family flips from "no" to
    "yes, with `always_up=false`".
- The reachability problem is real but narrower than B0182 claimed: these
  envelopes are reachable, and the barrier is that their conditions include
  options whose defaults differ from what the envelope requires, with nothing
  in the record naming them. That is a documentation and discoverability
  defect, not an architectural one — and it is far cheaper to fix.
- Recommended: record each automatic envelope's full option set, including
  non-default values it requires, alongside its qualification. B0075's record
  names the stages and the speedup but not `always_up=false`, which is the one
  thing a user needed.

Four-category record: `filters.normal`/`eigenvalues`/`covariancefeatures` as a
composed family are confirmed automatically selected and reachable at 10.134x
on the named 1M shape with `always_up=false`; no code changed.

## B0184 — The reconstruction was in the repo: four of six compose envelopes reach

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `aa176e20f`; no product code changes.
- B0183 found the eigen family reachable once `always_up=false` was supplied,
  and flagged that B0177's negative verdicts were built by hand-transcribing
  matcher predicates out of C++ and so were untrustworthy. This slice redid all
  six compose envelopes properly.
- **Method finding, and the real error behind B0177/B0182/B0183.**
  `test/data/pdg/placement-calibration-sm89.json` stores, under `pipelines`,
  the *exact pipeline each model was calibrated on* — `always_up: false` and
  all — for every one of the 35 models. Three benchmark slices reconstructed
  envelopes by reading `RuntimePlacement.cpp` predicates by hand when the
  authoritative, machine-readable answer was already committed. The
  reachability "defect" was substantially a failure to read the record.
- Six envelopes, every literal supplied, 1M fixture, complete-process wall
  clock through the public `pdg pipeline`, three runs, median:

| Envelope | Pinned PDAL | `pdg` | Speedup | Byte-exact | Resident executor |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | :-: | --- |
| eigen family | 14.450 s | 1.442 s | **10.021x** | yes | engaged |
| rank-optimal | 11.307 s | 1.446 s | **7.821x** | yes | engaged |
| approximate-coplanar + ferry | 4.129 s | 0.994 s | **4.153x** | yes | engaged |
| radiusassign (direct) | 1.650 s | 0.605 s | **2.728x** | yes | engaged |
| outlier + nndistance | 7.974 s | 0.335 s | **23.785x** | yes | refused |
| radius outlier + radialdensity | 5.952 s | 6.082 s | 0.979x | yes | refused |

- **Four of six engage**, not the three of seven B0177 reported. Two verdicts
  flip outright: rank-optimal from "no — mixed models" to 7.821x, and
  radiusassign, whose earlier attempt failed only because this slice first
  wrote `value` where the option is `update_expression`.
- The non-default options each envelope requires, which no prose record named:

| Envelope | Options whose defaults are wrong for it |
| --- | --- |
| eigen family | `normal.always_up=false` (default **true**), `eigenvalues.normalize=true` (default **false**), `knn=12` on all three (defaults 8/8/10) |
| rank-optimal | `estimaterank.knn=14` (default 8) |
| radiusassign | `is3d=true` (default **false**); the option is `update_expression`, not `value` |
| radius outlier + radialdensity | `radius=1.01` on both (default 1.0) |

- `outlier + nndistance` is the slice's most interesting row: the resident
  executor **refuses** it, yet it still runs **23.785x** faster byte-exact. The
  automatic compose envelope is not the only accelerated route, so "envelope
  refused" must never be read as "no acceleration" — B0177 drew exactly that
  inference and it is unsound.
- Both refusals report `missing_calibration_model`, which is a fallback
  artifact: `filters.outlier` has no per-stage model, so when a compose matcher
  declines, the per-stage path finds nothing. Their calibrated pipelines match
  the reconstructions field for field, so the mismatch is on a **planner-derived**
  attribute the user cannot set — `deviceKnnGatherNeighbors`,
  `deviceQueryBytesPerPoint`, `preferredResidency`, `indexBuilds`, or a
  residency boundary. `PDG_DISABLE_KNN_DISTANCE_PREFILTER`,
  `PDG_DISABLE_NND_DEVICE_REPAIR`, `PDG_DISABLE_OUTLIER_DEVICE_REPAIR`, and
  `PDG_DISABLE_NEIGHBORHOOD_ROW_BOUNDARY` each leave the refusal unchanged, so
  it is none of those four.
- **Stopped rather than guessing further.** Three slices have now inferred
  matcher predicates without instrumentation, and two of the three were wrong.
  The tooling gap is the blocker: `--stats` exposes no compiled-plan
  introspection, so a declining matcher cannot say which predicate failed.

Four-category record: four of six compose envelopes are confirmed reachable and
automatically selected at 10.021x/7.821x/4.153x/2.728x byte-exact on the named
1M shape with the option sets above; one is refused yet 23.785x by another
route; one is refused and flat; no code changed.

## B0185 — All six compose envelopes reach; two B0184 refusals were my own artifacts

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: `bec9b8b50` plus one diagnostics-only addition to
  `src/cli/ResidentPipeline.cpp` (`compiledPlanJson`).
- B0184 could not explain why two envelopes refused and stopped rather than
  guess a fourth time. This slice built the instrument it said was missing and
  the instrument immediately showed **both refusals were measurement errors of
  mine, not engine defects.**
- **The diagnostic.** `--stats` now carries a `plan` section, emitted
  unconditionally, with the planner-derived attributes the compose matchers
  test: per stage `native`, `preferred_residency`, `resident_region`,
  `device_knn_gather_neighbors`, `device_query_bytes_per_point`,
  `device_index_build_bytes_per_point`,
  `device_to_host_bytes_per_input_point`, plus `resident_regions`,
  `index_builds`, `grid_builds` and the residency boundaries. It reads the
  compiled plan and changes no placement decision.
- It paid immediately: both refusing plans matched **every** predicate their
  envelope tests — `outlier + nndistance` at `gather=11`, `qbpp=133` on both
  stages, one region, one index build; `radius outlier + radialdensity` at
  `ibbpp=28/0`, `qbpp=4`, `d2h=4/0`, upload 0→1 at 24 B and spill 3→4 at 10 B.
  Nothing in the plan was wrong, which is what redirected the search to the
  admission path.
- **Error one — the stats did not describe the run I timed.**
  `runResidentPipelineImpl` takes an `automaticAdmission` parameter: **false**
  for an explicit `pdg resident` invocation, **true** when routed from `pdg
  pipeline`. These two envelopes are gated behind facts set only under
  automatic admission, so my `pdg resident --stats` probe disabled the very
  route my `pdg pipeline` timing exercised. B0184 read `executor` and
  `unavailable_reason` from one mode while reporting a speedup from the other.
  That is why `outlier + nndistance` was recorded as "refused, yet 23.785x": it
  was never refused. The eigen family and rank-optimal were unaffected only
  because their matchers run unconditionally in `RuntimePlacement.cpp`.
- **Error two — a JSON array where the envelope requires a string.**
  `experimentalResidentRadiusOutlierRadialDensityAssignEnvelope` tests
  `assign.at("value").is_string()`. B0184 wrote `"value": ["UserData = 1 WHERE
  RadialDensity >= 0.2"]`; the calibration file records it as a bare string.
  With that one change:

| | Pinned PDAL | `pdg pipeline` | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| radius outlier + radialdensity | 5.835 s | 0.327 s | **17.846x, byte-exact** |

  Against a recorded 15.897x — it *exceeds* the record.
- **Six of six compose envelopes reach**, byte-exact: 10.021x, 7.821x, 4.153x,
  2.728x, 23.785x, 17.846x. B0177's "three of seven" and B0184's "four of six"
  are both superseded. **No envelope in this family was ever unreachable.**
- The whole reachability defect, tracked across B0176, B0177, B0182, B0183,
  B0184 and this slice, reduces to: envelopes are matched on **exact JSON
  document text** — key counts, scalar-versus-array, and options whose defaults
  are the opposite of what is required — and nothing in the record named those.
  The calibration file did, all along.
- Two standing method rules, both learned the hard way here:
  1. Never read `--stats` from `pdg resident` to explain a `pdg pipeline`
     timing. They are different admission modes. Prefer instrumenting the
     invocation actually being measured.
  2. Reconstruct envelopes by copying the calibrated pipeline out of
     `test/data/pdg/placement-calibration-sm89.json` **verbatim**, including
     scalar-versus-array shape. Do not retype it.

Four-category record: all six compose envelopes are confirmed reachable,
automatically selected and byte-exact on the named 1M shape; `--stats` gains an
unconditional compiled-plan section; no placement decision changed.

## B0186 — The reference pipelines get nothing: a policy, not a capability, refuses them

- Recorded: 2026-08-12.
- Source state: clean commit `4b6528dcd`; no product code changes.
- With reachability closed (B0185, D0215), this returns to D0208's actual
  release criterion: the six reference pipelines in
  `bench/pipelines/reference/`, measured by
  `scripts/pdg/benchmark_reference.py` against pinned PDAL on the 1M LAZ
  fixture, complete-process wall clock, alternating order, three runs.

| Pipeline | Pinned PDAL | `pdg` | Speedup | Byte-exact |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | :-: |
| r6 features | 9.096 s | 9.069 s | 1.003x | yes |
| r4 denoise + thin | 4.599 s | 4.629 s | 0.993x | yes |
| r2 ground normalize | 1.558 s | 1.565 s | 0.996x | yes |
| r3 DTM | 0.654 s | 0.672 s | 0.973x | yes |
| r1 translate | 0.481 s | 0.526 s | 0.915x | yes |
| r5 COPC query | 0.247 s | 0.269 s | 0.917x | yes |

- **Every one is byte-exact and every one is at or below parity**, while the
  six compose envelopes measured yesterday reach 2.728x to 23.785x. This is the
  D0208 gap stated as a number: the fork is fast on calibrated shapes and
  worth nothing on the workflows it was reprioritized to serve.
- **Fixed admission tax.** A 10,000-point translate — essentially no work —
  costs pinned PDAL 23.9 ms and `pdg` 40.7 ms. Process startup is not the
  cause: `--version` is 15.8 ms for PDAL and **14.0 ms** for `pdg`. The
  difference is admission machinery, paid per pipeline whether or not anything
  is placed. Disabling CUDA by any of five routes lands at ~33.9 ms, so it
  splits into **~7 ms of CUDA discovery and ~10 ms of non-CUDA overhead**.
- That tax explains the short pipelines and not the long ones: r1 +45 ms, r5
  +22 ms, r3 +18 ms, r4 +30 ms, r2 +7 ms, r6 −27 ms. Re-running with
  `PDG_ENABLE_CUDA=0` recovers r1 0.915x→0.940x and r5 0.917x→0.930x but
  leaves r3 unchanged at 0.973x, so **removing CUDA discovery entirely would
  still not reach parity** — there is a residual non-CUDA regression.
- **The finding that matters is r6.** It carries 9.1 s of neighborhood work —
  `filters.normal(knn=8)` then `filters.covariancefeatures(knn=8)` — and gets
  1.003x, while the calibrated eigen family gets 10.021x on the same hardware.
  Two controls isolate the cause:
