## B0269 — Parallel `readers.las` record unpacking in streaming and standard modes

Date: 2026-08-15 UTC. Same reference workstation, CUDA 13.3 Release tree,
pinned oracle `ea66f6a9...`, frozen epoch, and fixtures as B0268. Scope
decision: D0269. Final launcher `879fdccc...` (unchanged), engine
`69e4e557470f32a3...`, shared library `399f5a805481a455...` (full values in
the handoff anchors).

### Attribution and change under test

Sibling-`pdal` probes on the reference LAS/LAZ (best of three, streaming):
process startup 0.018 s; 1M-point LAS to `writers.null` 0.134 s; LAZ to
`writers.null` 0.160 s; LAS to LAS 0.181 s (after B0268). The reader's
7-worker tile pool already reads and decodes in parallel; the ~0.11 s per
million points left on the main thread was `LasReader::processOne`'s
per-record `loadPoint` (18-plus typed `setField` calls per record) — the
mirror image of B0268's serial packing, present in twelve of the fourteen
headlines.

`readers.las` now unpacks decoded records on a fixed-slot
`hostworkers::HostSlotPool` (at most eight slots, `rowWorkerCount` policy,
2,048-row minimum) in both modes. The streaming executor gains an opt-in
reader hook, `Streamable::readStreamBatch(table, pointLimit, read)`
(default false; `read < pointLimit` means end of input exactly as a false
`processOne()` would); `LasReader` implements it and its standard `read()`
takes the same shape per tile. Tile consumption is unchanged and serial
(same order, same waits, same `queueNext()` cadence): each tile contributes
a contiguous run of records with the rows they fill, tiles stay alive until
the workers join, standard mode appends the rows serially first, and the
workers run `loadPoint` on disjoint rows. Small runs, streaming `start`
(pinned PDAL's eof accounting hangs there in streaming — reproduced, not
fixed), and the read callback stay serial. Sources `io/LasReader.cpp`
`95198d4b7b13e3cc...`, `io/LasReader.hpp` `342f1d42da4d78f8...`,
`io/private/las/Tile.hpp` `9a8f5f0240b16522...`, `pdal/Streamable.{hpp,cpp}`
`c884092a484cc5d0...`/`546b46025c00d586...`,
`tests/differential/las_reader_unpack_matrix.py` `c7c240fbf080fb2e...`,
`tests/unit/las_reader_unpack_test.cpp` `7e1a7a637f4b30c2...`.

Same-binary probes after the change (sibling `pdal`, best of three): LAS to
`writers.null` 0.134 s -> 0.054 s streaming and 0.147 s -> 0.072 s
standard; LAZ to `writers.null` 0.160 s -> 0.088 s / 0.174 s -> 0.090 s;
LAS to LAS 0.181 s -> 0.097 s / 0.191 s -> 0.112 s; the
`PDG_DISABLE_HOST_NEIGHBORHOOD_WORKERS=1` control reproduces the prior
figures (0.133 s, 0.159 s, 0.282 s with the writer also serial).

### Test-first exactness proof

A new pinned-oracle reader matrix (`pdg_las_reader_unpack_matrix_pinned_exact`,
30 cases; fixtures written by the pinned oracle from generated text;
candidate delegating to the forked sibling; three forced unpack workers):
formats 0/1/2/3/6/7/8, LAS and LAZ, LAS 1.4 extra-bytes VLRs, LAS 1.2
named and `use_eb_vlr` extra bytes, 120,000-point multi-tile fixtures,
`count`, `start`, downstream `filters.range` skips, a 700-point file, the
disable control and natural policy, in streaming and `--nostream` modes,
through LAS 1.4/format-8 `extra_dims=all` and 17-digit `writers.text`
sinks — all exact. A test-only `PDAL_TEST_TRACE_LAS_UNPACK=1` trace proved
the path per case (three 10,000-row batches or 50,000/20,000-row tile runs;
the 700-point file serial). `LasReaderUnpack` runs a 15,000-row stream
table over 123,457 points so a batch spans two tiles (two segments in one
worker run) and matches the serial control and standard mode byte-for-byte.
The B0268 writer matrix, r14 conversion matrix, and LAZ chunk units pass.

## B0270 — Ordered parallel COPC tile decode under `requests=1` (r5)

Date: 2026-08-15 UTC. Same reference workstation, CUDA 13.3 Release tree,
pinned oracle `ea66f6a9...`, frozen epoch, and fixtures as B0269. Scope
decision: D0270. Final launcher `879fdccc...` (unchanged), engine
`be40417afebcfc6dacd8821fd73cecd0e7e1125d6c3097d11fcfca300c4bbf59`, shared
library `456adf3f7b0f8c9205f422a6e3d679421c8fd9a1c66a48ca97fe4d9830fcb668`.

### Attribution

r5 was the last headline at parity (1.023038x warm in the B0269 suite).
Sibling-`pdal` probes on the reference COPC query (bounds + resolution 1.0,
`requests=1`, 280,130 points selected from 26 overlapping nodes; best of
three): the query to `writers.null` costs 0.236 s of the 0.243 s process
(startup 0.018 s); the same query with eight request threads reads in
0.081 s but emits tiles in an unpinned completion order, which is why the
reference pins `requests=1`. With one thread the connector fetch and the
lazperf decompression of every selected node ran serially while the
consumer waited; `filters.stats` (about 0.03 s on 280K points) and the
writer were hidden behind that wait.

### Change under test

`copc::Tile::read()` is split into `fetch()` and `decompress()`. Under
`requests=1` the fork keeps exactly one request thread (the connector sees
the same serialized fetches, in hierarchy order, with keep-alive
backpressure counted on fetched-but-unconsumed tiles) and hands each
fetched tile to a decode pool (at most eight threads,
`hostworkers::rowWorkerCount` policy and controls); decoded tiles wait in a
sequence-keyed map and `read()`/`processOne()` pop the next tile in fetch
order. Points, order, the first erroring tile's diagnostic, and status equal
pinned PDAL's; `requests` above one keeps the pinned unordered path;
`PDG_DISABLE_HOST_NEIGHBORHOOD_WORKERS` restores the pinned single-thread
path. Sources `io/CopcReader.cpp` `1f952f6913aa2fe4...`, `io/CopcReader.hpp`
`153907dd4e7ad12e...`, `io/private/copc/Tile.{cpp,hpp}`
`beb0ac8e2de5cc0d...`/`da42eafa575019e3...`,
`tests/differential/copc_reader_matrix.py` `460a1e9b6424b1e4...`. Sibling
probes after the change: the query to `writers.null` 0.236 s -> 0.098 s, the
full 1M read 0.318 s -> 0.171 s, the r5 graph 0.247 s -> 0.144 s (its
`filters.stats` pass, 0.03 s, is now exposed); the disable control
reproduces the prior figures.

### Test-first exactness proof

A new pinned-oracle COPC reader matrix (`pdg_copc_reader_matrix_pinned_exact`,
19 cases; the fixture is a 1.2M-point, 21-node COPC written by the pinned
oracle with `threads=1,fixed_seed=true` from generated text; candidate
delegating to the forked sibling): full, bounds (17 nodes), bounds +
resolution, resolution (5 nodes), polygon (19 nodes), `count` (1 node), an
empty selection, `keep_alive` 2 (more nodes than the window), the disable
control, and a two-worker cap, in streaming and `--nostream` modes, through
LAS and 17-digit text sinks — all exact. A test-only
`PDAL_TEST_TRACE_COPC_DECODE=1` trace proved the path per case (ordered
decode with eight workers, or the pinned single-thread path for the
control). The r14 conversion and hybrid reader matrices pass. Finding: under
UBSan the vendored lazperf point14 predictors report int32 wraparound while
decoding this fixture (design of the LAZ integer coder, shared with pinned
PDAL, output byte-identical); the sanitizer differential lane now carries a
`vendor/lazperf`-scoped UBSan suppression (`tests/sanitizers/
ubsan-lazperf.supp`) so fork code stays instrumented and vendored arithmetic
does not fail exact stream comparisons.

## B0271 — `--fast` tie-order contract: device tie choices stand, no CPU tie repair

Date: 2026-08-15 UTC. Same reference workstation, CUDA 13.3 Release tree,
pinned oracle `ea66f6a9...`, frozen epoch, and fixtures as B0270. Scope
decision: D0271 (maintainer request). Final launcher `0c7a844b902ad93a4fcabf8fb15eb715ac15bae1d8a019d18f3bd7744298ec13`,
engine `cc0a490d506506fbbfbe1cbf43753155d80c97a0c5498c9f69ae3b7c6fec4cb5`, shared library `456adf3f7b0f8c92...` (unchanged from
B0270).

### Change under test

`pdg::knnStatusMask()` (`include/pdg/FastMode.hpp`, `src/core/FastMode.cpp`)
clears `KnnDistanceTie` whenever the launcher-armed marker
`PDG_INTERNAL_FAST_MODE=1` is present. Both device gather kernels apply a
per-build `__constant__` mask (`src/index/SpatialIndexKernels.cu`
`d64b4b80c67f3aee...`) and the host-index paths apply the same mask
(`src/index/SpatialIndex.cpp` `791ee58d3f50a864...`), so under `--fast` no
identity-observing consumer runs its exact host tie repair; incomplete
bounded searches keep their flag and repair. The launcher now consumes
`--fast` on every route including the environment-selected engine route
(`src/cli/DispatchMain.cpp` `daeba3df97b0f329...`; the injected-marker guard
strips only an ambient marker). The reference runner gains the D0271 fast
comparator (`scripts/pdg/benchmark_reference.py` `58983e0ebd5b7d7c...`:
record-by-record comparison against the first oracle artifact, identical
count/layout/coordinates, differing records bounded by
`--fast-max-differing-records-fraction`, `--candidate-arg`), and the suite
runner labels fast aggregates and refuses to mix contracts
(`scripts/pdg/reference_suite.py` `0ef6526134b41a0a...`).

Sibling probe on the r6 graph (best of three): `pdg` 0.879 s -> `pdg --fast`
0.763 s; 25 of 1,000,000 records differ (coordinates identical), against
2,343 tie-flagged rows in the exact run — most ties do not change the
published normal or features because the device and nanoflann agree on the
set and order, or the tied candidates are equivalent.

### Proof

`FastMode` (marker -> mask; host index reports ties only under the default
contract, ids/distances/other bits unchanged, both backends),
`CudaSpatialIndex.RelaxedTieOrderMasksOnlyTheTieBitOnBothBackends` (device,
both backends, bitwise distances), `PdgNeighborClassifierFilter.
RelaxedTieOrderSkipsTheHostRepairUnderFast` and `PdgApproximateCoplanarFilter.
RelaxedTieOrderSkipsTheEigenRepairUnderFast` (no repair, differing rows
bounded by the exact ambiguous count), `pdg_fast_tie_contract_cuda` (exact
repair proven under `PDG_REQUIRE_NEIGHBORHOOD_TIE_REPAIR`; `--fast` fails
closed under the same gate with the named diagnostic and publishes nothing;
`--fast` records keep count/layout/coordinates; default byte-identical),
`pdg_dispatcher_process_boundary` (environment route), and
`pdg_reference_runner_environment_contract` (comparator accepts a bounded
attribute difference only under fast within the allowance, rejects
coordinate changes and reordering under both). Compute Sanitizer memcheck,
racecheck, initcheck, and synccheck over the changed gather kernels
(`CudaSpatialIndex` relaxed-tie, unique-host-order, and masked-ground
units): 0 errors, 0 hazards.

## B0273 — Banded parallel raster accumulation in `writers.gdal` (r3, r7)

Date: 2026-08-15 UTC. Same reference workstation, CUDA 13.3 Release tree,
pinned oracle `ea66f6a9...`, frozen epoch, and fixtures as B0272. Scope
decision: D0273. Final launcher `abd3cbe9c08535a9...` (unchanged), engine
`6de500c5ece48a2eb914f36c241edf7300d47eb1e751ee2570042e9663d40c34`, shared
library `5a602f7d5f651d824a52b4c9b73f06aead78b239e0faf0d8a83927ce1bf1e102`.

### Attribution

Sibling prefix probes on the r3 graph (best of three): LAZ read 0.105 s;
+ SMRF 0.274 s (`PDG_DEBUG_SMRF_PHASES`: obj_mask 0.050, zimin_and_fill
0.044, classify_ground 0.032, zipro_and_fill 0.028, segment_returns 0.021,
return_zero_scan 0.012, the rest under 0.006 each); + range 0.285 s; +
`writers.gdal` (IDW, 1 m, dynamic bounds, standard mode) 0.416 s. The
0.13 s raster accumulation is a serial per-point radius walk whose per-cell
folds are order-dependent only within a cell. On r7 (streaming, fixed
bounds, bin-mode max) the writer costs about 0.02 s.

### Change under test

`GDALGrid::addPoint(x, y, z, rowBegin, rowEnd)` (`io/private/GDALGrid.cpp`
`5f03747cc016c082...`, `.hpp` `c5885e331f9f2de3...`) performs the pinned
quadrant walk but updates only cells whose row lies in the band;
`GDALGrid::rowSpan` gives a conservative superset of the rows a point can
touch. `GDALWriter` (`io/GDALWriter.cpp` `6aa39a57874e3c26...`, `.hpp`
`6af15272c670845e...`) buckets each point, in order, into the list of every
band its radius can touch and replays each list on its own pool slot (at
most eight bands, one per slot, `rowWorkerCount` policy and controls), in
`writeView` after the grid is created from the view bounds and in a new
`processStreamBatch` override for fixed grids and bin mode; a streaming grid
that grows point by point in radius mode keeps the per-point path because
pinned PDAL's walk reaches only the cells that exist when each point arrives
(cells added by a later expansion never receive earlier points — reproduced,
not fixed); percentile bins (a per-cell hash map) stay serial. Sibling r3:
0.416 s -> 0.319 s (the same-binary disable control, which also serializes
the reader and SMRF, is 0.670 s); sibling r7 with the writer's banding
alone switched off (`BandMinimumRows` raised) 0.167 s vs 0.170 s on — bin
mode's single-cell update has nothing to gain, and the batch overhead is
within noise.

### Test-first exactness proof

A new pinned-oracle GDAL writer matrix (`pdg_gdal_writer_matrix_pinned_exact`,
19 cases; candidate delegating to the forked sibling; three forced band
workers on a 30,200-point scatter with a dense edge strip and 200 exact
duplicates): dynamic and fixed grids, `all`, `idw` (power/radius), `mean,
stdev,count`, `max` bin mode, `min`, window fill, percentiles, a non-Z
dimension with float32 output, upstream `filters.range` skips, a large
radius, bounds clipping most points, both execution modes, the disable
control, and the natural policy — raster bytes and metadata, streams, and
status all exact. A test-only `PDAL_TEST_TRACE_GDAL_BANDS=1` trace proved
the path per case (banded runs for standard mode, fixed grids, and bin
mode; none for streaming dynamic radius grids or percentiles). Two
divergences found and fixed during the slice: the streaming dynamic-grid
interleaving quirk above (initially reordered, one cell in 875 KB differed
from pinned) and a concurrent insertion into the percentile hash map (now
serial by policy).

### Final-binary qualification (nine pairs per state)

## B0274 — Concurrent, structure-identical nanoflann builds for every KD index

Date: 2026-08-15 UTC. Same reference workstation, CUDA 13.3 Release tree,
pinned oracle `ea66f6a9...`, frozen epoch, and fixtures as B0273. Scope
decision: D0274. Final launcher `abd3cbe9c08535a9...` (unchanged), engine
`c7afa7ba2d596562c7d23f04d9a22d13fecee9f5ed8a8e2c3556438338e2fd26`, shared
library `ea113c56be1498e81088c8900f6c15bf86a2deec34c8a3dfccebd440597084d7`.

### Attribution

`pdg-engine resident r6 --stats` after B0273: the exact eigen tie repair
(2,343 rows) costs 0.155 s, of which 0.109 s is building the private
cached KD3 tree (nanoflann leaf 100) — 0.004 s is the repair itself. The
same serial build appears once in r11 and r4 (host outlier), in HAG-NN's
compatibility ground index, LOF, and SMRF's KD2 fills.

### Change under test

`vendor/nanoflann/nanoflann.hpp` (`fad9880b620e3523...`) gains
`divideTreeConcurrent` — the same recursion, `middleSplit_`, and bounding
boxes as `divideTree`, node allocation serialized through one mutex, and the
left child of a node built on a `std::async` thread while the count stays
below `n_thread_build` (`set_build_threads`); `pdal/private/KDImpl.hpp`
(`d1df91caad9eeb48...`) sets it from the shared host-worker policy (at most
eight; trees under 256 points stay serial; the disable control restores the
serial build) for `KD2Impl`, `KD3ImplT`, and `KDFlexImpl`, and fills the
cached KD3 snapshot on fixed row chunks. The tree is a deterministic
function of the points, so structure, leaves, split values, and therefore
every query's node order and tie order are unchanged. Engine probe: the r6
repair tree 0.104 s -> 0.058 s (0.070 s from the concurrent build alone;
the snapshot fill was the rest); the critical path — the root's serial
partition and each level's — bounds the gain.

### Test-first exactness proof

`Kd3Concurrency.ConcurrentBuildProducesTheSerialTree`: kNN ids, squared
distances, and radius results identical between the one-thread build and
2/3/5/8-thread builds on tie-dense modular fixtures (12K and 130K points)
and a 12,800-point integer lattice whose k=8 cuts through equal-distance
groups. Every pinned-oracle matrix that forces three workers now also
forces three build threads: r11 (27 cases), SMRF, outlier, HAG, LOF, sample,
reprojection lanes all exact against pinned PDAL. A first cut tripped the
`PDAL_TEST_REQUIRE_HOST_NEIGHBORHOOD_WORKERS` hook on a four-point KD2 tree
in the SMRF matrix; trees under 256 points no longer consult the policy.

## B0276 — Scale ladder on a datacenter GPU: 47M / 95M / 190M points on an H200

Date: 2026-08-16 UTC. Scope decision: D0276. Product binaries unchanged
(source tree `4c8f03c13`; product sources identical to B0274/B0275). This
record answers the maintainer's question "are we even faster compared to
stock PDAL on the largest workflows?" with measurements, not code.
Report section 7b of `docs/reports/b0275-cross-machine-benchmark.html`
(`b31f3d9d9ba807c0...`, regenerated with `--ladder-results`).

### Machine (Vast.ai, one instance, destroyed after the archive was downloaded)

NVIDIA H200 141 GB (driver 580.159.03), 2x Intel Xeon Platinum 8480+
(224 threads visible; **container cgroup quota `cpu.max 2687999 100000`,
i.e. about 26.9 cores** — the host-parallel paths were throttled to roughly
the Threadripper box's core budget), 3 TB RAM, image
`nvidia/cuda:13.3.1-devel-ubuntu24.04`. Oracle: upstream PDAL 2.10.0 at
`f1e35f5c` built on the box (`a0ab6c637190d74e...`, same bytes as the B0275
box oracle). Fork built by `bench/remote/vast_bootstrap.sh` with
`PDG_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=90` (`pdg` `eb22979e2b1c6c3d...` and library
`442660700670a47b...` identical to the B0275 box build; engine
`5273e79e475a5c17...` differs only by the SM 90 device code). Automatic CUDA
selection stays profile-locked to the qualified RTX 4090, so the kNN graphs
ran with `PDG_EXPERIMENTAL_CUDA_HYBRID=1`; the I/O-bound graphs ran the
default host configuration.

### Inputs

AHN4 GeoTiles (`geotiles.citg.tudelft.nl/AHN4_T/`): 25GN1_01 as-is
(47,478,228 points, 480 MB LAZ); 01+02 merged with `pdg` (`filters.merge`,
93,886,838 points, 541 MB); 01–04 merged (190,083,571 points, 1,088 MB) —
`bench/remote/vast_ladder.sh`, `results-ladder/inputs.txt`. All LAS 1.4
format 8, EPSG:28992.

### Results (warm, one pair per cell, `benchmark_reference.py --runs 1 --warmups 0`; every row byte-exact incl. stdout/stderr/status)

| Workload / configuration | 47M pinned / PDG | Speedup | 95M pinned / PDG | Speedup | 190M pinned / PDG | Speedup |

| r14 laz2las default | 23.7 / 7.3 s | 3.258x | 42.2 / 12.2 s | 3.457x | 87.4 / 24.0 s | 3.647x |
| r1 translate default | 28.0 / 17.5 s | 1.606x | 53.0 / 38.2 s | 1.389x | 111.1 / 73.1 s | 1.520x |
| r3 dtm default | 27.5 / 17.1 s | 1.611x | 50.0 / 31.7 s | 1.577x | 109.5 / 67.7 s | 1.617x |
| r2 ground normalize CUDA hybrid | 108.7 / 77.5 s | 1.403x | 229.8 / 150.3 s | 1.529x | 416.1 / 252.7 s | 1.646x |
| r4 denoise thin CUDA hybrid | 247.6 / 25.4 s | 9.744x | 485.2 / 47.7 s | 10.173x | 1002.0 / 107.3 s | 9.342x |
| r6 features CUDA hybrid | 558.1 / 53.6 s | 10.403x | 1117.0 / 107.6 s | 10.380x | 2225.4 / 213.6 s | 10.420x |

| r6 features default (host) | 562.9 / 280.7 s | 2.005x | — | — | — | — |

Peak RSS (pinned / PDG): r6 CUDA 7.1/13.7 GB, 12.5/25.4 GB, 25.2/51.1 GB at
47/95/190M; r2 CUDA 5.7/6.5, 9.6/10.9, 19.3/22.0 GB; r4 CUDA 5.3/5.5,
9.0/9.1, 18.1/18.1 GB; r3 within 0.1 GB of pinned; r14/r1 about 0.1–0.2 GB.
Reports `build/benchmarks/b0276-h200/results-ladder/ladder-*.json`
(`366529ce0d48a5d0...` 47M r14 … `086bf055976a6d92...` 190M r2; 20 files,
plus `merge.json`, `machine.txt`, `inputs.txt`, per-run logs; archive
`results-b0276.tar.gz`).

### Reading

- The kNN-heavy graphs sit on a **flat ~10x plateau** across 47M–190M
  (r6 10.40/10.38/10.42x; r4 9.74/10.17/9.34x): pinned PDAL is one core doing
  N kd-tree queries and PDG is the device doing the same N queries plus the
  host doing the exact repairs, so both sides scale about linearly and the
  ratio stays where the kernel throughput puts it. Bigger inputs do not raise
  the ratio; the large device keeps the ratio from breaking down at sizes
  where a 24 GB card would have to tile (the 190M r6 run holds 51 GB
  resident on the host).
- r2 (ground + normalize) is the only graph whose speedup climbs with size
  (1.40 → 1.53 → 1.65x): its GPU-eligible share (kNN/HAG) grows relative to
  the fixed host-only PMF ground filter.
- I/O-bound graphs stay flat at their single-file LAZ decode/encode ceiling:
  r14 3.26 → 3.65x, r1 1.4–1.6x, r3 ~1.6x. They do not exceed the
  Threadripper box's rows because this container had about the same core
  quota (26.9 cores) — the extra 197 visible threads were not usable.
- Compared with the RTX 4090 box at 47M (r6 CUDA 13.6x, r4 12.0x) the H200's
  ratios are lower, not higher, and PDG's absolute times are not better
  (r6 53.6 s on the H200 vs 48.3 s on the 4090 box vs 30.7 s on the
  workstation; r4 25.4 / 24.9 / 15.5 s; r2 77.5 / 81.8 / 45.9 s) while the
  pinned baseline is faster per core than the Threadripper's (r6 558 vs
  658 s). Interpretation, not measured: at these sizes the device is not the
  bottleneck for these graphs — the exact host repair, the single-file LAZ
  decode/encode and the host-side stages are — so a larger GPU changes
  little and a faster single core lowers the ratio.

### Validation and caveats

- No product code changed; the B0274 lanes stand. New files:
  `bench/remote/vast_ladder.sh`; `bench/remote/vast_bootstrap.sh` now fetches
  the oracle commit shallowly with retries (the full clone hit "early EOF" on
  this host); `bench/report/build_report.py` gained the `--ladder-results`
  section.
- One run per cell (no spread); the pinned side alone needed up to 37 minutes
  per run at 190M, which is why the ladder is not three-pair.
- Two H100 NVL offers were rented and destroyed before this box without
  producing results (one with an unfixable sshd `authorized_keys` mode
  error, one that went offline). The H200 (contract 47864532) ran about
  3.3 hours; the account credit went from $98.72 to $84.53 across the three
  instances (about $14.2), i.e. about $15.5 of the authorized ~$100 spent in
  total (B0275 + B0276). No instances remain.

## B0277 — `pdg calibrate` on two rented machines: default mode before and after a local placement profile

Date: 2026-08-16/17 UTC. Scope decisions: D0277 (the command and the
profile), D0278 (the resident layout follows a file's extra-bytes dimension
types). Report: `docs/reports/b0277-local-calibration.html` (`70af7351bac1356c...`,
generated by `bench/report/build_calibration_report.py`; published as a
private artifact). Product change on the reference machine: none in behaviour — the
embedded profile takes precedence there and `pdg calibrate` declines without
`--force`; the exact suite claim of record stays B0274.

### Local validation (reference workstation)

- Unit: `tests/unit/local_profile_test.cpp` (8 tests: schema round trip and
  rejection, lookup statuses, embedded-key precedence, override scoping,
  residual fit sign split, synthetic cloud determinism/LAS layout,
  `DimensionRegistry::redefineType`), also under ASan/UBSan (host-sanitize
  tree, 8/8).
- Process: `pdg_calibrate_local_profile_cuda_exact`
  (`tests/differential/calibrate_test.py`, 15.3 s): status/dry-run write
  nothing; the reference machine declines without `--force`; a quick
  calibration (normal-covariance and LOF at 100K/250K, one pair) admits only
  byte-exact device wins; the local profile makes the automatic route select
  the resident device path (proof gate exit 0) while a missing profile, a
  profile keyed to another machine and the calibration override fail closed
  (124); default output with the profile equals the host output and the
  pinned oracle; D0278: a file carrying `Deviation=uint16` runs on the
  device route byte-identically to host/oracle, a file carrying `Rank=uint16`
  under `filters.estimaterank` is refused by the preflight with the
  device-computed reason and completes on the host byte-identically.
- Aggregates after both changes: CUDA Release `ctest -j1 -E corpus`
  **858/858** (21 documented optional skips, 540.87 s); Host Debug
  **550/550** (4 optional skips, 233.25 s); placement audit unchanged
  (214/218 with the shared fitting code).
- 47,478,228-point AHN4 tile, plain feature graph on the resident device
  executor with a widened local profile (test hook hides the embedded one):
  23.1 s vs 156.9 s host on the same machine, output byte-identical to the
  pinned oracle (`0a1d3255af93f31f...`).

### Rented boxes (Vast.ai; two instances run concurrently, both destroyed after download)

| | RTX 4090 box | RTX 5090 box |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GPU / driver | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 24 GB, 580.95.05 | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 32 GB, 580.159.03 |
| Host | 2x AMD EPYC 7742 (255 threads visible; offer 32 effective cores) | 2x AMD EPYC 7B12 (256 threads; cgroup `cpu.max 3072000 100000` = 30.7 cores) |

Protocol (`bench/remote/vast_calibrate.sh`, then `vast_calibrate_post.sh`
after the `--append` merge fix, then `vast_calibrate_post2.sh` after D0278):
`pdg calibrate --status` (host path); the fourteen reference workflows in

the same suite in default mode, calibrated; the same suite with the CUDA
hybrid forced; a real-data calibration on the 1M reference fixture for
comparison; the AHN4 47.5M tile in default mode.

LOF at 48M synthetic points on the 24 GB card ran the resident executor
(tiled) and stayed exact. Real-data calibration (1M reference fixture at
250K/1M, 4090): the same models within a few tenths of the synthetic
ratios (compose 2.23x/3.93x, lof 3.70x/8.72x, nndistance 1.57x/3.72x,
eigen-family 3.46x/5.45x) except `radiusassign` (0.78x/1.59x vs
1.96x/3.88x — the synthetic return-number mix differs from real data), which
is why the documentation recommends `--input` with the user's own tiles.

dimensions dropped, default mode was already 14.7x/14.9x (features) and
22.4x/25.4x (LOF); after D0278 (engine rebuilt on the boxes,
`vast_calibrate_post2.sh`) the original tile itself runs on the resident
device executor in default mode: features 10.09x/14.79x, LOF 22.10x/25.46x,
byte-exact against the box oracle, with the same peak PDG RSS as the EB-free
tile (14.7 GB / 9.4 GB). The 4090's features cell (78.9 s vs 53.7 s on the
EB-free tile and 52.3 s on the 5090) is a single run and is reported as
measured. The r6 reference graph keeps its `extra_dims=all` bound (host at
47M on every machine, D0277).

### Validation and caveats

- Product changes: `pdg calibrate` and the local profile (D0277); the
  resident layout following file EB types (D0278). Both are outside the
  reference machine's default path (embedded profile precedence; the
  reference suite fixtures carry no mismatched EB dims), so B0274 stands.
- Box measurements are single-calibration, three-pair suite figures on
  containers with CPU quotas; the two boxes ran concurrently on separate
  hosts. Only same-box comparisons are exact.
- Two defects found and fixed during the run, both before checkpoint: the
  device path of the point-program models refused to overwrite an existing
  output (outputs are now removed before every run, as the reference runner
  does), and the first `--append` replaced an appended model's fit and
  envelope with the new sizes only (it now refits over every size in the
  profile's evidence, so envelopes only grow); the box suites measured under
  the defective profile are retained as `suite-1m-default-calibrated-appendbug`
  (numerically an uncalibrated repeat).
- The synthetic calibration cloud is a stand-in; `radiusassign` shows why
  `--input` matters.
- Vast: contract 47893469 (4090, $0.335/h, about 5.1 h) and 47893981
  (5090, $0.361/h, about 4.9 h); earlier attempts (a 4090 with the sshd
  `authorized_keys` mode defect, fixed for the reruns by an on-start
  permission loop; a 5090 whose image pull stalled) were destroyed within
  minutes. Credit went from $84.53 to $80.55 (about $4.0 for this record;
  about $19.5 of the ~$100 authorization spent in total across
  B0275–B0277); no instances remain.

## B0278 — Drop-in defaults: shipped GPU-class profiles from a ten-GPU sweep, a generic fallback, and default mode with nothing calibrated

Date: 2026-08-17 UTC. Scope decision: D0279 (shipped GPU-class profiles,
the generic fallback, `pdg calibrate` as the tightening tool, the
`normal-covariancefeatures-compose-extradims` model). Report:
`docs/reports/b0278-drop-in-defaults.html` (`9c24476e9c98e7a1...`,
generated by `bench/report/build_sweep_report.py`). Product change on
the reference machine: none in behaviour — the embedded reference profile
still takes precedence (`active_profile_tier: embedded`; a
`shipped-rtx4090-sm89-cuda13.3` profile and the generic profile are present
but not consulted there), so the exact suite claim of record stays B0274.
Session note: this record was assembled after the driving session lost its
connection mid-run; the RTX 3090 box (the last one) was found still running
with both phases complete, its results were pulled and it was destroyed.

### Protocol

Ten Vast.ai boxes, one per GPU class, each bootstrapped from the D0279
working tree (`vast_bootstrap.sh`, `nvidia/cuda:13.3.1-devel-ubuntu24.04`,
upstream PDAL 2.10.0 oracle built on the box). Two phases per box:

1. **Sweep** (`bench/remote/vast_sweep.sh`): `pdg calibrate --status` and
   the fourteen reference workflows at 1M in default mode with no profile
   ("before"); `pdg calibrate` (16 models incl. the new extradims case;
   250K/1M/4M, three pairs; synthetic cloud), then `--append` at 16M and 48M
   (48M only on cards with ≥ 24 GB) for the four big-cloud models
   (`normal-covariancefeatures-compose`, `…-extradims`, `lof`,
   `nndistance`, one pair each); the same suite with the local profile; the
   AHN4 47.5M tile in default mode with the local profile (features plain,
   r6 reference graph, LOF plain) on the cards that measured big sizes.
2. **Proof** (`bench/remote/vast_sweep_proof.sh`): the local profiles were
   converted on the workstation by `bench/report/make_shipped_profile.py`
   (margin 3x) into `data/placement-profiles/*.json` plus the generic
   profile, uploaded, embedded by a rebuild on the box, the local profile
   removed, `pdg calibrate --status` checked for `active_profile_tier:
   shipped`, and the same fourteen workflows run in default mode as a fresh
   user would — no environment, no calibration — plus the AHN4 features
   cells on the big cards. On three boxes (A10, RTX 3060, RTX 4080) the
   box's own shipped profile was excluded from the embedded set so the box
   exercised the **generic** tier (`active_profile_tier: generic`, AHN4
   skipped).

Every cell in every phase — 3 suites x 14 workflows x 10 boxes, 3 generic
suites, 30 AHN4 cells, and every calibrate pair — was byte-identical to the
box oracle. All ten shipped profiles regenerate identically (modulo
timestamp) from the archived `results-sweep/placement-profile.json` files;
the generic profile likewise from the ten shipped ones.

  the margin by 0.016 — so its shipped envelope begins at 4M, r6 at 1M
  stays on the host, and the shipped suite differs from "before" only by
  that box's host-side noise (its host-only workflows moved by up to 20%
  between the two host-only runs: r5 1.24 → 0.99 → 1.23, r9 1.63 → 1.33 →
  1.35). Its local profile, which admits 1M at 2.98x, reaches r6 8.66x.
- **RTX 3090** (ten-core Xeon E5 v4 host): every ratio is roughly half of
  the other boxes' (compose 2.5x at 1M, 2.7x/2.3x at 16M/48M), so the
  shipped profile admits only eigen-family, estimaterank, fused-point-
  program, LOF, nndistance, radiusassign and rank-optimal, and the compose
  model only at 4M: r6 stays host at 1M (3.16x is noise around 2.27x) and
  the AHN4 tile stays host (below). The margin refused thin wins on
  purpose; `pdg calibrate` on that box admits them (r6 not measured at 1M
  there, AHN4 8.1x/8.2x).
- The **generic** tier is inert on the fourteen workflows at 1M on all
  three boxes (every workflow within run-to-run spread of "before"): its
  admitted models begin at 4M except `eigen-family-compose` (1M),
  `rank-optimal-compose` (1M) and `lof` (250K), none of which the r-suite
  reaches at 1M. Its device use is proven by the process test (applies
  inside its bounds, inert outside) and it was **not** measured on a big
  cloud — the drop-in promise for an unlisted GPU is "never slower than the
  host path at 1M, device only where every swept class won by 3x".

### Expected effect, from existing measurements

No box was re-rented. The B0278 proof (3x set) is the measured floor of the
new set on every class; each box's local-profile suite and AHN4 runs
(margin 1 — a superset of the 1.7x admissions with the same coefficients)
are the nearest evidence for the wider admissions and are all in B0278: RTX
5090 r6 **8.66x** at 1M under the local profile (2.44x under the 3x set);
RTX 3090 AHN4 features **8.06x**, r6 graph **8.18x**, LOF **18.77x** under
the local profile (2.38x / 2.52x under the 3x set); on no box did the local
profile make the fourteen-workflow suite slower than the host path beyond
run-to-run noise. The single-feature filters at 1M (measured 2.2x–3.6x on
the EPYC/Xeon hosts, 1.7x–2.3x on the 3090's) are new admissions no suite
workflow reaches on its own — the r-suite composes them — so their 1M
behaviour is covered by the calibrate pairs (byte-exact, three pairs each)
and not by a workflow run.

## B0280 — Independent audit repair: the 35.98M VEIL r6 route is exact and 14.697x after embedded-profile refresh

Date: 2026-08-17 EDT. Decision: D0281. Machine: AMD Ryzen 9 7900 (24 logical
CPUs), NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (SM 8.9, 24,564 MiB), driver 610.43.03, CUDA
13.3. Candidate: base commit `89b6f753aa316c0bd935bc12826c575f62f7e812`
plus the D0281 worktree changes; binary SHA-256
`154b1960d51be92a7c8c4be78a9387ca0d01b395f4652020f21086215443faf3`
for the public launcher. The accepted VEIL pair pins candidate engine
`40d8df8b779ef51651c5f70928bce01daedf2ac87c92c6149ee32fbb86c7fcdc`;
the final bounded-layout AHN4 pairs pin engine
`c3a1511b4db5f4ad66c251d1b84571978226785b90478e6795f48260c3dc0541`.
The post-measurement plain-layout/provenance hardening build validated below is
engine `c450519ce15e6029c4b4b4b6a7a354d31bf8a604333ca31e0d59d4b283a62b87`;
no new timing is attributed to that later binary.
All three pin fork PDAL shared library
`ea113c56be1498e81088c8900f6c15bf86a2deec34c8a3dfccebd440597084d7`.
Oracle: a separately built clean upstream PDAL 2.10.0 checkout at pinned commit
`f1e35f5c3e416b8c6a2c39966c8205cfae54afe2`, binary SHA-256
`804a7b160fe57bf6294afb2204e1891cb4f6ad567e56d965bc76479f872cc013`
and shared-library SHA-256
`0117e264c16bf45f84e9bc1b0eea163edbab643d2e5d8baa98bc55287d617e4e`.

### Root cause and test-first repair

The original independent blind report selected embedded profile
`sm89-2026-08-07-pre-p1.5-matrix` and measured 303.165 s upstream versus
118.724 s candidate (**2.554x**). Placement refused the device composition as
`mixed_calibration_models`: the exact-machine embedded profile took precedence
over the shipped RTX-4090 profile but lacked
`normal-covariancefeatures-compose-extradims`; its plain composition also
stopped at 4M while the shipped profile carried both shapes to 48M. This was
profile shadowing, not a CUDA error, memory refusal, unsupported LAS format, or
resident exactness failure.

The regression was written first: a VEIL-sized 35,976,465-point format-6/30
byte input with a format-7/100 byte compressed `extra_dims=all` sink must select
the separately named device composition, and the embedded record must carry
every same-class shipped model name. Those tests failed against the old
profile. D0281 then refreshed the embedded model and bounded its envelope by
independent exact-machine rows through 47,478,228 points. The runtime gate now
admits only formats 6--8, input widths through 63 bytes, and output widths
100--127; legacy, waveform, undersized, and wider records are negative controls.
The enlarged plain model is independently limited to its two exact physical
pairs: uncompressed format-7/36 input or compressed format-8/44 input, each to
uncompressed format-7/36 output.
The compiled placement audit rejects models with no recorded case or explicit
upper envelopes beyond their largest recorded device-winning case, and a
registered provenance test requires the retained reports, verifies their hashes,
and binds exactness, timings, point/layout facts, profile, pipeline/input/output
hashes, and the required-route switch back to the calibration cases.

### Accepted complete-process measurement

Harness: `scripts/pdg/benchmark_reference.py`, exact contract, warm cache, zero
warmups, one alternating measured pair, frozen epoch 1704067200. Pipeline:
`bench/pipelines/reference/r6-features.json`. Input: local VEIL LAZ,
266,539,183 bytes, 35,976,465 points, format 6 / 30-byte records, SHA-256
`73fb5a0e6d3fffe3a2c82f91ff9ee50b88475f65d94805db498d64d987ddbe3f`.
The candidate environment included
`PDG_REQUIRE_AUTOMATIC_NORMAL_COVARIANCE_RESIDENT=1`; a silent fallback would
therefore fail rather than produce a timing.

| Process | Wall time | Peak RSS | Output |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| clean pinned upstream | 313.165909 s | 4,919,758,848 B | 2,178,019,955 B |
| repaired default `pdg` | 21.308468 s | 10,321,358,848 B | 2,178,019,955 B |

Complete-process speedup: **14.696782x**. Artifact bytes, stdout, stderr, and
exit status were identical. Both outputs contain 35,976,465 points and have
SHA-256 `c0a0f44f80e01c9a31cf57b0f2cda8f328c6cb4a8afeedafd55c27fefe9ba36b`.
An explicit resident telemetry pass independently reported `choice=device`,
one selected region, profile `shipped-rtx4090-sm89-cuda13.3`, input/output
record widths 30/100, and executor `planner_resident_shared_index`; the final
official pair reported active embedded profile
`sm89-2026-08-17-r6-large-layouts`. Raw report:

## B0282 — Hardened VEIL/AHN4 qualification: exact automatic routes at 13.192–17.521x

Date: 2026-08-17 EDT. Decision: D0282. Machine and clean oracle are the same
as B0280: AMD Ryzen 9 7900, RTX 4090 (SM 8.9), driver 610.43.03, CUDA 13.3,
and separately built upstream PDAL commit
`f1e35f5c3e416b8c6a2c39966c8205cfae54afe2`. The oracle executable is
`804a7b160fe57bf6294afb2204e1891cb4f6ad567e56d965bc76479f872cc013`
and the library actually resolved by its loader is
`0117e264c16bf45f84e9bc1b0eea163edbab643d2e5d8baa98bc55287d617e4e`.
The final candidate launcher is
`cf5470c6c065756e038823bf1c668903a7786de5149e125c6b05bab7e4b2d410`,
engine `452a8029b62792e3cad56f7322666b78a7aff7d46983304a4cec83334c59d5d0`,
and actually loaded fork library
`ea113c56be1498e81088c8900f6c15bf86a2deec34c8a3dfccebd440597084d7`.

An independent re-review found that B0280's forward harness could omit loader
provenance if `ldd` failed, while its retained-report verifier did not require
the new component roles. The harness now fails closed for an ELF candidate
without an ELF `pdg-engine` and for either real executable without a resolved
`libpdalcpp`. It scrubs ambient `LD_*`, records any explicit reintroduction,
and generates the physical qualification block itself. The retained verifier
requires one candidate engine, one loaded library per process, valid component
hashes, the loader scrub, and all prior exactness/layout/route bindings.

The first hardened AHN4 plain attempt also exposed an environmental failure
worth retaining: accumulated derived files left `/tmp` under pressure, PDAL's
unchanged writer produced a 528,801,792-byte partial LAS with an unfinalized
header and nevertheless returned zero. The exact benchmark contract rejected
the result; no speed claim was accepted. After removing only reproducible
derived audit outputs, a candidate-only reproduction emitted the full
1,709,218,507-byte file with the clean-oracle hash. Automatic resident
execution now parses the published LAS/LAZ header and VLR/EVLR extents before
returning success; uncompressed outputs also prove the complete point-record
extent. A deterministic truncation injection in the physical selection matrix
must return nonzero with `automatic resident LAS publication is invalid`.

## B0283 — Rejected full-LAZ-redecode publication guard

Date: 2026-08-17 EDT. Decision: D0283. A read-only review correctly identified
that D0282's compressed publication check could accept a LAZ truncated after
some point payload. The first correction streamed and decoded every declared
point after the writer had already encoded the same output. It was correct but
not acceptable on the timed default route.

On the B0282 machine/oracle and VEIL r6 case, the route-proof candidate remained
byte-exact but took 69.848751 s versus 312.547894 s upstream: **4.474638x**.
The extra full decode cost about 49.6 seconds relative to B0284's structural
guard on the same candidate route and erased most of the acceleration. This
implementation was rejected before updating the active placement evidence.

profile, and the required automatic-resident proof switch.

## B0284 — Final chunk-table guard: exact automatic routes at 13.441–17.996x

Date: 2026-08-17 EDT. Decision: D0283. Machine, pinned upstream commit, oracle
executable/library, candidate launcher, and loaded fork library are unchanged
from B0282. The final candidate engine is
`1e6d3319e3e054b798c11a07cb078453b1cd89693d97b4c673331c9f2271a046`.

The accepted LAZ publication guard parses the LASzip VLR and chunk table,
requires the table to cover the declared point count, and requires its relative
chunk byte sizes to cover exactly the compressed point-payload extent. It is
O(chunks), not O(points). The physical selection matrix's deliberate
mid-payload truncation is rejected nonzero, while the full valid LAZ check is
effectively lost in run-to-run noise.

### Conformance, COPC, and `pdg verify`

The first frozen diagnostic conformance run is rejected as release evidence:
its runner accepted 92 matching nonzero process outcomes, including 16
matching aborts. The hardened runner requires a declared status and the matrix
was corrected so all cases are valid successful executions. The qualifying
frozen-binary rerun passed **2,048/2,048** cases with zero unexplained
differences and all 4,096 product executions returning zero. Manifest SHA-256:
`e0d880fcd33413fc4d2daae67b4ada4bb189d964664dfbe771a1637c65468a1f`;
raw report SHA-256:
`1453f7afaa2ad8846db4eba83b3c15c73b323e7db21811c68e91a0510745e824`;
gzip SHA-256:
`6ba382ffbec6eeae9186c861a7331bfdf72d8138d47e4af4823ec24202ef16bf`.

A real one-million-point pinned-PDAL COPC pair proves byte nondeterminism:
container SHA-256 values differ, while the canonical full-record digest
`40f0919627ac9f02e9d9311fb54b9c347980dbd7667d1741768b882bad133f51`,
semantic metadata, hierarchy invariants and exact center query agree. Physical
hierarchy assignment and the coarse preview differ and remain reported as
diagnostics. Accepted semantic report SHA-256:
`94e348cc24c1dd38a2768df248c1d3b8c566a97d8bd64724b183dccb4a1d465b`.

The packaged author-run `pdg verify` artifact on the RTX 4090 is exact and
valid, detects no binary drift, and records
`external_validation.status = not-performed`. Its small 250K fixture honestly
measures **0.785296x**. JSON SHA-256:
`961bcb72f869d6ed186232b1a6ab5205051f487335c595e587d0a71dada7d124`;
HTML SHA-256:
`928ee06296b427783df88c46e82ae147f62d1a7622807f8dc83947fd2c392cee`.

Two deployment attempts failed preflight before accepted aggregate timing:
one used a wrong COPC fixture; the next lacked required GDAL/PROJ runtime
tools. Both were rejected. Vast credit moved from `50.7409784967` to
`42.4604191779`, so the complete re-proof cost about **$8.28**, well below the
estimated $22. Raw reports, machine/profile facts, manifests and checksums are
published under `docs/reports/b0286-frozen-reproof/`.

No 3DEP catalog was selected or timed and no unrelated party was contacted.
This entry proves the frozen artifact on the named machines and fixtures; it
does not prove the preregistered population claim or third-party validation.
